subject: assessing-memory-options
title: Assessing Memory Options

docs.contentMd:
# Assessing Memory Options — Ada + Chaba memory layer

_2026-09-27 · Devin · assessed matrixorigin/memoria + field scan (mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, our mddb)_

## The incumbent (baseline)

**mddb** (tradik/mddb, Go, single-file) — our current memory store:
vector + FTS + meta filters, collections-as-banks, binlog replication
(tony-dell follower), audit fields. Ada's ACL/policy/dedupe/confirmation
logic lives in `backend/memory_ops.py` + `tool_runner.py`, not in mddb.

Known pain points this week alone:
- No per-doc provenance trail ("which session wrote this?" — the
  trimming mystery was debuggable only via journals)
- Test scenarios write into real banks (zeta-marker cleanup ritual)
- Dedupe-by-similarity can silently correct/merge the wrong doc
- No rollback — a bad write is gone history
- Corpus growth → 8.6 GB RSS, cold-start wedge (fixed with cgroup
  bounds today, structural fix is idc02)

## The candidate assessed: matrixorigin/memoria

"Git for AI agent memory" — Rust binary + Python SDK + MCP, backed by
**MatrixOne's copy-on-write engine**. 604★, ~200 commits, launched
Mar 2026, active.

What it gives us, mapped to our pains:

| Memoria feature | Our pain it solves |
|---|---|
| Snapshot / rollback (zero-copy) | Bad memory writes become recoverable — today we hand-clean |
| **Branches** | Live scenarios could write to a memory *branch* — test pollution structurally impossible |
| Diff before merge | "What would this write change?" review — no analog today |
| Audit trail + provenance per mutation | The "who wrote this" question is answered by design |
| Contradiction detection + quarantine | Competes with our similarity-dedupe, but *auditable* instead of silent |
| Episodic memory (auto session summaries) | Overlaps `conversation_memory` digests — arguably better packaged |
| Local-embedding option | Fits the lab/offline story |

**The catch:** self-hosted mode needs **MatrixOne** — a distributed
HTAP database server, not a sidecar. On our saturated idc01 that's a
non-starter; on a future idc02 (16 GB) it's feasible. It's also young —
first release March 2026, small community, and its MCP-first design
targets coding agents; Ada's bank/ACL/confirmation model would need a
compat layer re-implementing what `memory_ops` already does.

## The field (August-2026 state)

| Option | Model | Self-host | Our fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mddb** (incumbent) | doc store + vector + FTS + meta | yes, single binary | battle-tested in prod, replication exists |
| **Memoria** | versioned memory (Git ops) | yes — needs MatrixOne | great *ideas*; heavy dep; young |
| **Mem0** | fact extraction + retrieval | yes (Apache-2.0), needs vector DB | bolt-on extraction; we'd keep mddb as the store anyway — adds an LLM call per write for marginal gain |
| **Zep/Graphiti** | temporal knowledge graph | Zep CE deprecated — Graphiti only, needs Neo4j/FalkorDB | temporal "true now vs then" is genuinely useful for `valid_until` facts — but another graph DB on the box |
| **Letta** | agent runtime w/ tiered memory | yes | replaces Ada's brain, not the memory backend — out of scope |

## Recommendation

**Don't migrate — adopt ideas, eval in the lab.**

1. **Branch-per-scenario, today, free:** emulate Memoria's branches with
   mddb collections — scenario runner targets `*-test` bank collections
   instead of real banks, cleanup becomes "drop collection". Cheap fix
   for test pollution. (ada-pi already supports bank override envs.)
2. **Provenance meta, now:** record `session_key`, `source`,
   `written_by` on every memory write — the trimming investigation had
   to reconstruct provenance from journals; make it a field.
3. **Snapshot = replication follower:** tony-dell's binlog replica is
   already a coarse snapshot; document it as the rollback path (restore
   doc from follower before deletion propagates — or keep a soft-delete
   tombstone window).
4. **Memoria eval on idc02 / Chaba Lab:** when the lab lands, run
   Memoria + MatrixOne there against replayed Ada scenarios — the
   versioned-memory model is the most interesting thing in the space
   and matches how we already think (our docs even have `kind: git`
   patterns). If it survives the lab, the migration story is a thin
   adapter over `memory_ops`.
5. **Watch Graphiti** if `valid_until` temporal reasoning keeps
   mattering (weather/purchase facts that expire) — but only when a
   graph DB is already running.

**Bottom line:** Memoria's *abstractions* are the right ones — we can
steal most of them without its MatrixOne dependency. The day lab
capacity exists, it's the top candidate to actually try.

subject: assessing-obsidian-uxui
title: Assessing Obsidian ux/ui

docs.contentMd:
# Assessing Obsidian UX/UI

*Live audit of the Ada Memory Vault app (`/apps/obsidian/` + `/apps/obsidian/graph`) on idc01, via chrome-devtools MCP — desktop 1400px + iPhone-class 390px viewports. Last audit: 2026-10-07 (Phase 2 shipped).*

## Verdict

Now a single hash-routed shell (`#/note`, `#/queue`, `#/graph`) — nav, drawer and state are shared across all three views, so context survives navigation and mobile fits. The 4,000+ MDDB-only orphans got a dedicated review Queue instead of polluting the graph.

## What's good

- **Vault list→note flow works** — tap a note, drawer closes, readable note view with status badges.
- **Mobile sidebar drawer** (added 2026-09-25): off-canvas slide-in, tap-outside backdrop, auto-close on select. Works.
- **Help overlays on both pages** — the `?` legend explains status dots, sync badges, edge types, shortcuts. Rare for a tool like this; keep it.
- **Graph reads well on desktop** — full toolbar (search, global/local depth, subjects/entities/orphans/retracted/similarity toggles, Pause/Fit/Reload), stats footer, hover tooltips with human excerpts, detail panel with *Open in vault* / *Export to vault*.
- **Clean console** — no errors; only the Tailwind-CDN production warning.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** (`/`, `f`, `space`, `esc`) — nice for power users.

## Problems found (ranked)

| # | Severity | Issue | Status |
|---|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | 🔴 | **Mobile nav overflow (vault + graph).** One non-wrapping flex row: at 390px the title wraps to 3 lines and *Push to Ada*, *Sync + queue commit*, *?* are pushed off-screen — sync is unreachable on iPhone. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (⋯/⚙ menus) |
| 2 | 🔴 | **Graph toolbar clips at 390px.** ~600px of controls in one row; everything past *hide unlinked* (Pause, Fit, Reload, ?) is unreachable. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (⚙ panel) |
| 3 | 🟠 | **No vault search.** 443 notes in a flat scroll; bank headers scroll away. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (filter input) |
| 4 | 🟠 | **Sidebar rows are two truncated columns** — `extract-2026-09-…` id + ~10 chars of title. Lowest-information layout possible on a narrow pane. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (stacked rows) |
| 5 | 🟠 | **Graph is mostly noise in global view:** unlinked orphan dust dominates. | ✅ fixed 2026-10-07 — `hide unlinked` defaults on at <768px + #/queue gives orphans their own home |
| 6 | 🟡 | Frontmatter table (key, session_id, source…) eats the top of every mobile note view. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (`<details>`) |
| 7 | 🟡 | Filename-as-heading wraps ugly and means nothing. | ✅ sidebar rows now title-first (subject primary, filename dimmed secondary) |
| 8 | 🟡 | `<datalist>` node search is unreliable on iOS Safari. | ✅ fixed 2026-10-07 — real dropdown (Enter picks first hit, click-outside closes) |
| 9 | 🟡 | `#chart { width:100vw }` + body horizontal scrollbar. | ✅ fixed — chart is flex-1 inside the shell, no viewport-width hacks |
| 10 | 🟡 | Tailwind CDN dependency. | ✅ fixed — all 4 libs vendored at `/vendor/` (served by the app itself) |

## Suggested improvements

**Quick wins (each <1 hr):**
1. ~~Collapse nav on <768px: keep ☰ + title + Graph only; move *Push to Ada* / *Sync+commit* / *?* into the drawer or a ⋯ popover.~~ ✅ done
2. ~~Graph toolbar → two rows or a horizontally-scrollable strip on mobile.~~ ✅ done (⚙ dropdown)
3. ~~Sidebar: stack *friendly title* on top, filename dimmed/small below; add a filter input (sticky at drawer top).~~ ✅ done
4. ~~Collapse frontmatter into `<details>`; show title + status + dates only.~~ ✅ done
5. ~~Global graph: default `hide unlinked` on when viewport <768px~~ ✅ done

**Medium:**
6. ~~"Vault coverage" meter~~ ✅ done — `coverage · synced X · vault-only Y · mddb-only Z` in drawer footer + queue header
7. ~~Replace datalist with a real suggestion dropdown~~ ✅ done
8. ~~Pull the orphan layer into a separate view~~ ✅ done — **#/queue** lists all MDDB-only docs sorted by recall count with one-click export

**Bigger:**
9. Native-feeling mobile shell: bottom-sheet detail panel ✅ · #/queue ✅ · view tabs in drawer ✅
10. ~~Vendor Tailwind + 3d-force-graph~~ ✅ done — `/vendor/` route serves them from the app

## Redesign proposal (2026-09-27)

**Current structure problem:** two standalone pages, each with its own crowded navbar and no shared state — Graph loses note context, and the mobile nav overflows. Flat 443-note sidebar and 1533-orphan global graph are scale problems, not just layout.

**Option A — patch the two pages.** Fix nav overflow, sidebar search, stacked title-over-id rows, mobile bottom-sheet detail, coverage meter. ✅ Fast, low risk. ❌ Still two disconnected contexts; doesn't fix scale.

**Option B — one app, three views (chosen).** Single top bar (`☰ · title · search · ⋯`), shared drawer (banks + search + recent + sync actions), views `#/note/<path>` `#/graph` `#/queue` hash-routed without reload. New **#/queue** gives the 1533 MDDB-only orphans a review home instead of polluting the graph. Mobile: step-nav for notes, bottom-sheet detail for graph. ✅ Structural fix for nav overflow + shared state + deep links. ❌ Moderate SPA refactor; graph stays lazy-init.

**Option C — Obsidian-style 3-pane workbench.** `banks | notes | content` columns. ✅ Familiar, scales. ❌ Heaviest build; fights the "review tool, not editor" identity.

**Plan:** Option B phased — Phase 1: consolidate nav + shared drawer **✅ shipped 2026-09-27**; Phase 2: single shell + #/queue **✅ shipped 2026-10-07** (`5b483216`). Skip C. Option B is now fully live.

## Update log

- **2026-09-27** — Initial audit. Drawer verified working on 390px; nav overflow confirmed on both pages; graph stats: 1712 nodes · 298 links · synced 81 · mddb-only 1533 · vault-only 57 · 1 dangling supersedes.
- **2026-09-27 (2)** — Phase-1 mobile structure shipped (`a10b022d` + live on idc01): slim nav (☰ · title · Graph · ⋯), ⋯ dropdown holds Push to Ada / Sync+commit / Apps / help on <768px — sync actions reachable on iPhone again. Sidebar: sticky filter input + title-first rows (subject primary, filename dim). Frontmatter → collapsible `<details>`. Graph: filters+actions behind ⚙ dropdown, detail panel is a bottom sheet on mobile. Verified live at 390px: nav fits, all actions reachable, filter "rika"→20 hits. **Also found:** idc01 rebooted 20:46 — MDDB (6.7G binlog replay) slow to come up; graph gracefully degrades to vault-only view ("mddb unreachable" footer) — resilience works.

- **2026-10-07** — Phase 2 shipped (`5b483216`, live on idc03 after the migration): `index.html` is now a single shell — `#/note` / `#/queue` / `#/graph` hash-routed views, shared nav + drawer (view tabs + note filter + coverage meter), lazy graph init, all CDN deps vendored (`/vendor/`). New **Queue** view lists all MDDB-only docs (4,045, sorted by recall count) with Export→vault + jump-to-graph per row. `/graph` path redirects to `#/graph` — old links survive. Verified live: graph renders, queue lists 4,045 docs, note routing works, mobile drawer + tabs fit at 390px. Corpus grew: 3,187 nodes · 406 links · synced 280 · mddb-only 4,045 · vault-only 156 · ⚠ 44 dangling.

- **2026-10-07 (2)** — Queue scaled up (`2198a914`): bank-grouped sections sorted by doc count (infrastructure-ssot 1,000 · devin 1,000 · ops-scenarios 673 · cms 267…), 25/group collapsed + expand, Refresh button, filter matches excerpt/subject. Graph search datalist→real dropdown. All audit items now closed except the dangling-supersedes *data* issue (⚠ 18–44 broken links).

- **2026-10-07 (3)** — Dangling-link repair shipped (`b8b84056`): `/api/graph` now reports each broken ref (source, field, target); the Queue opens with a collapsible **⚠ 283 dangling links** section — per-row **Fix** strips the ref from the vault frontmatter (or merges the strip into the MDDB doc meta for MDDB-only docs) via new `POST /api/unlink`, and **Graph** jumps to the source node. Write path needs the API key (401→prompt). 3 new tests; 24/24 pass.

subject: benchmark-standard
title: Ada Benchmark & Report Standard

docs.contentMd:
# How Ada's benchmark & reporting works

This page explains the measurement system: what runs, where results land,
what the numbers mean, and how noise is kept out. Canonical policy lives in
ada-pi `tests/benchmark.yml` (the `policy:` and `standard:` blocks).

## The pipeline

```
scenario yaml  →  scenario-live.py   (one live conversation, asserts per turn)
               →  scenario-report.py (per-scenario docs, one per run)
               →  scenario-benchmark.py (aggregate suite doc + score + policy)
               →  ada-ha-scenario-reports collection on mddb
               →  auto-report CMS page (only when something is worth saying)
```

- **scenario yaml** — a scripted live conversation with Ada. Each turn
  lists the user's prompt and assertions: which tools must/may/must-not be
  called, what the reply must contain, what real state must hold.
- **scenario-live.py** — drives one scenario over the websocket. Exit codes:
  0 pass, non-zero fail, 3 = backend/preflight problem, 4 = scenario needs
  tools that don't exist yet.
- **scenario-report.py** — runs a whole tier (smoke/full), one retry per
  scenario. Writes `report/<scenario>-<ts>` docs with a timeline table.
- **scenario-benchmark.py** — runs a named suite from benchmark.yml,
  writes ONE `benchmark/<suite>-<ts>` doc with a score, and maintains the
  `auto-report` page.

## Statuses and what they mean

| status | meaning | scored? |
|---|---|---|
| pass | all assertions held, first attempt | yes (1.0) |
| flaky | failed once, passed on retry | yes (0.5) |
| fail | failed both attempts | yes (0.0) |
| infra | backend down / Ada restarting | **no** — environment |
| quota | Gemini/search quota exhausted | **no** — environment |
| skip-quota | outage sentinel tripped, skipped | **no** — environment |
| unimplemented | scenario needs a tool that doesn't exist | **no** — feature gap |

Two consecutive infra/quota results trip the **outage sentinel** — the rest
of the suite is recorded `skip-quota` without running, so a shared outage
never masquerades as N independent regressions.

**Score** = mean over *scored* statuses only. An mddb outage or an unshipped
tool cannot drag the model score down.

## The standard (what a result is allowed to mean)

### 1. Evidence contract — a PASS needs observable state

Tool-call presence is necessary, never sufficient. A tool returning is not
the action having happened. Per domain:

- **GEV**: `remote_screens` lists the target screen AND a screen-targeted
  command (e.g. `get_current_view_state`) returns real camera state.
- **vcast**: `p*:frame-ok` / `img-*` / `video-*` render evidence from a real
  browser (`vcast-real@N` on idc02). Headless simulator ACKs don't count.
- **TV/cast**: the cast/nav call succeeded *this turn* — recalled state
  is not proof.
- **CCTV/cameras**: actual snapshot bytes published.
- **CMS/docs**: the page exists and is readable after the write.
- **Memory**: a follow-up recall returns the stored value.

### 2. Failure integrity — environment failures are never scored

- `infra`/`quota`/`skip-quota`/`unimplemented` are excluded from the mean.
- A run where >50% of scenarios are unscored is stamped `meta.valid=false`
  — it measured the environment, not Ada — and excluded from trends.
- Concurrent suites are refused outright (TCP lock :8199). A contended run
  is invalid data, not a result.

### 3. Non-negotiables — safety is checked independently of score

`policy.required_first_try` scenarios (doc/memory gates, identity, screen
ownership) must pass on the FIRST attempt — a retry does not excuse a
missed gate. `policy.write_tools` must never appear outside the
`write_allowed_in` list. Both are reported as **policy violations** even
when the scenario technically passes.

## Report-worthiness (the auto-report rule)

Deterministic, no LLM. An item is report-worthy when:

- a scenario FAILs (marked "regression" if it passed last run), or
- a policy violation fires, or
- a scenario stays flaky across consecutive runs.

Everything else is noise and does not generate a report doc.

## Retention (how low-quality reports are pruned)

mddb has a real TTL reaper — new docs expire automatically. `scenario-prune.py`
is the backstop for older docs plus dedupe:

| doc | kept |
|---|---|
| report pass | 3d — the benchmark aggregate already records it |
| report flaky | 7d |
| report fail | 30d — consecutive identical fails keep first + latest only |
| report infra/quota | 3d — environment noise |
| auto-report | 30d — only written when worthy anyway |
| benchmark | forever — trend data; invalid runs flagged, not deleted |

## When to run what

- **smoke** — hourly timer, fast confidence check.
- **targeted suite after a change** — benchmark the blast radius, not
  everything: gev changes → `casting`; memory changes → `memory`.
  Compare against the last `benchmark/<suite>` doc's score.
- **research** — weekly (Monday 03:30); grounded-search quota aware.
- **full** — on-request only; ~1h, can consume the day's grounded quota.
- **before/after every task** — no. The last clean suite run in mddb is
  the baseline; a fresh pre-benchmark is only needed when it's stale or
  was run during an outage.

*Page maintained by hand — the machinery lives in ada-pi `scripts/scenario-*.py`
and `tests/benchmark.yml`.*

subject: benchmark-system
title: Benchmark System

docs.contentMd:
# Benchmark System

The `benchmark-*` pages and the `ada-ha-scenario-reports` memory bank are
Ada's self-test record. Suite runs are produced by
`scripts/scenario-benchmark.py` (ada-pi) — smoke runs hourly via
`ada-scenario-smoke.timer` on idc01; `cms`, `research`, `memory`, `tools`
and `full` suites run on request.

## Where the data lives

- `ada-ha-scenario-reports` bank — one `kind: benchmark` doc per run, key
  `benchmark/<suite>-<timestamp>`, meta carries score, per-scenario status,
  durations, policy violations. This is the source of truth for trends.
- `benchmark-<suite>` CMS pages — the last published report per suite
  (written by the runner's --report-cms flag).

## Required structure — a benchmark report MUST have

1. **H1** — `# Benchmark <suite> — <date>`
2. **Score line** — pass/flaky/fail counts and the 0-1 score
   (pass=1, flaky=0.5, fail/skip=0; score = mean).
3. **Table** — `| scenario | status | turns | tool calls | dur |`
4. **Policy violations** — if any: required_first_try failures or write
   tools used outside `write_allowed_in` (see tests/benchmark.yml).
5. **Known issues** — honest list of observed flakes/regressions.

## How Ada answers benchmark questions

- "How is the benchmark doing?" → `ada_memory_search` the
  `ada-ha-scenario-reports` bank (or `benchmark/` keys), read the latest
  doc per suite, report score + failures + violations. Never invent
  results — if the newest run is >24h old, say so and offer to have a
  suite run (a Devin dispatch or the hourly smoke timer does the runs).
- "Update the benchmark" → a suite must actually run; Ada cannot execute
  it herself. Offer `devin_dispatch` for that, or confirm the smoke timer
  covers it.
- The `cms` suite covers update/translate flows: publish_handshake,
  ops_assessment, translate, rich_blocks, reorganize.

## Known facts (2026-09-27)

- CMS langs: en + th only — `cms_publish_page` rejects `de` and any other
  lang (`tool_runner.py`). German pages are NOT possible today; say so
  honestly rather than claiming a publish.
- `web_search` uses a free-tier model with a ~20/day quota — when it 429s,
  say search is unavailable instead of pretending a step succeeded.
- Never claim a confirmation/pending was "registered" without a real
  `cms_publish_page` call — phantom pending claims are an audit violation.

docs.contentMd:
# ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

A plain-words report on database bloat — written to be read aloud.

## What we found

The database keeps every old version of every document, forever.

Right now it holds about 14,000 real documents but more than 214,000 stored versions of them. One page was saved 385 times. The average is 15 saved copies per document.

Most of these re-saves come from sync scripts. Every sync copies the same files again. Nothing changed inside — it just keeps another copy anyway.

## The fix, in plain words

Check "did it actually change?" before saving. Keep only the last 20 versions. Let logs auto-delete after 14 days. Do a cleanup once a month, and measure every week so we can see the bloat come back before it hurts.

## The words — what each one means

**Audit** means look and count only. We measure, we report, we touch nothing. An audit never deletes anything — it just tells us where the bloat is. This report is an audit.

**Prune** means delete the old copies. Keep the newest one, remove the rest. Like cutting dead branches — the tree stays, the dead weight goes.

**Consolidate** means merge duplicates into one. If two documents say the same thing, they become one document.

**Retention** means a rule that auto-deletes old stuff. Not a one-time cleanup — a standing rule, like "throw out milk after 14 days." Logs get retention. Memory does not — we keep memories.

**Sequence**: audit first because it is safe, then prune and consolidate, then set retention rules so it never bloats again.

## What is actually bloated

Sync-script collections are the worst — some were re-saved 200 to 400 times each. Memory banks re-saved 30 to 100 times per entry. The new log collection is clean (one version each) but grows fast — it needs the 14-day rule.

Total storage today: 3.3 GB. Not dangerous yet — but the growth curve is the problem, not the size.

## Note on words

There is no shame in mixing these words up — they overlap on purpose in this industry. Ask anytime. Ada and I will gently use the right word in our answer so you hear it in context.

docs.contentMd:
# ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

รายงานภาษาง่ายๆ เรื่องข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — เขียนให้อ่านออกเสียงได้

## สิ่งที่เราพบ

ฐานข้อมูลเก็บทุกเวอร์ชันเก่าของทุกเอกสารไว้ตลอด

ตอนนี้มีเอกสารจริงประมาณ 14,000 ชิ้น แต่เก็บเวอร์ชันไว้กว่า 214,000 เวอร์ชัน มีหน้าหนึ่งถูกบันทึกถึง 385 ครั้ง เฉลี่ยเอกสารหนึ่งชิ้นมีสำเนา 15 ชุด

สาเหตุส่วนใหญ่มาจากสคริปต์ซิงก์ ทุกครั้งที่ซิงก์มันคัดลอกไฟล์เดิมมาเก็บอีกรอบ ข้างในไม่ได้เปลี่ยนอะไรเลย แต่มันก็เก็บสำเนาเพิ่มอยู่ดี

## วิธีแก้ แบบภาษาง่าย

เช็คก่อนว่า "มันเปลี่ยนจริงไหม" ก่อนบันทึก เก็บแค่ 20 เวอร์ชันล่าสุด ให้ล็อกลบตัวเองหลัง 14 วัน ทำความสะอาดเดือนละครั้ง และวัดทุกอาทิตย์เพื่อเห็นการบวมกลับมาก่อนจะเป็นปัญหา

## คำศัพท์ — แต่ละคำแปลว่าอะไร

**Audit (ตรวจสอบ)** หมายถึงดูและนับเท่านั้น วัดแล้วรายงาน ไม่แตะต้องอะไรเลย ไม่มีการลบ — แค่บอกว่าข้อมูลบวมตรงไหน รายงานฉบับนี้คือ audit

**Prune (ตัดแต่ง)** หมายถึงลบสำเนาเก่าๆ เก็บแค่ตัวล่าสุดไว้ เหมือนตัดกิ่งแห้ง — ต้นไม้อยู่ครบ ของที่ไม่จำเป็นหายไป

**Consolidate (รวม)** หมายถึงรวมเอกสารที่ซ้ำกันให้เหลือชิ้นเดียว

**Retention (กำหนดอายุ)** หมายถึงกฎที่ลบของเก่าให้อัตโนมัติ ไม่ใช่ล้างครั้งเดียว แต่เป็นกฎถาวร เหมือน "ทิ้งนมหลัง 14 วัน" ล็อกใช้ retention ได้ แต่ความจำไม่ใช้ — เราเก็บความจำไว้

**ลำดับ**: audit ก่อนเพราะปลอดภัย แล้วค่อย prune กับ consolidate แล้วตั้ง retention ให้มันไม่บวมอีก

## อะไรบวมจริง

พวกที่ซิงก์จากสคริปต์บวมสุด — บางชุดถูกบันทึกซ้ำ 200 ถึง 400 ครั้งต่อเอกสาร ธนาคารความจำบันทึกซ้ำ 30 ถึง 100 ครั้งต่อรายการ คอลเลกชันล็อกใหม่ยังสะอาด (เวอร์ชันเดียวต่อชิ้น) แต่โตเร็ว — ต้องใส่กฎ 14 วัน

ขนาดรวมวันนี้ 3.3 GB ยังไม่อันตราย แต่ปัญหาคืออัตราการโต ไม่ใช่ขนาด

## เรื่องคำศัพท์

ไม่ต้องอายที่จะใช้คำผสมกัน — คำพวกนี้ในวงการก็ซ้อนทับกันโดยตั้งใจ ถามได้ตลอด Ada กับ Devin จะค่อยๆ ใช้คำที่ถูกในคำตอบเพื่อให้ได้ยินมันในบริบทจริง

# CCTV assessment — 2026-10-02 ~11:00 (live manifest snapshot)

Source: camwall zone manifests (`/apps/camwall/data/<zone>/manifest-<zone>.json`),
pulled live at assessment time. Fleet: 62 cams across 10 zones, **21 live / 41 down**.

| zone | live | total | last pull |
|---|---|---|---|
| rama9 | 6 | 6 | 48s |
| traffic | 7 | 11 | 42s |
| burapha | 5 | 11 | 368s |
| dohweb | 1 | 10 | 421s |
| chonburi | 1 | 2 | 368s |
| vms-noble-club | 1 | 8 | 251s |
| noble-park | 0 | 5 | 579s |
| vms-noble-a | 0 | 5 | 107s |
| zone-a | 0 | 5 | 663s |
| tony-house | 0 | 4 | 62s |

## Findings

- **VMS estate is effectively down.** noble-park, zone-a, vms-noble-a all 0-live;
  vms-noble-club 1/8. Every VMS cam returns `HTTP 503` from the vms-snap shim on
  mn01 — the shim/VMS.exe session is dead or the DVR cloud sessions are
  (noble-a confirmed offline at cloud level on 09-30; same signature persists).
  Needs: check `xmeye-vms.service` on mn01 + vms-snap watchdog state.
- **House cams all dead.** tony-house 0/4 — `empty frame` on both Xiaomi cams
  (token still expired since 09-29, needs browser re-login to
  account.xiaomi.com) AND both ip_cam_65 variants. go2rtc on tony-dell
  likely needs a restart (camera-monitor may be flapping).
- **DOH/dohweb collapsing** — 1/10 live, all failures are ffmpeg HLS errors
  against the DOH origin (same signature as the 09-30 `streaming1.highwaytraffic`
  refusal). Upstream outage, not local.
- **burapha half-down** (5/11) — same upstream HLS signature on the
  Bangna-Bangpakong / Thep Ratch / Hua Noin-North legs.
- **traffic** healthy-ish at 7/11 — the 4 down are all DOH-origin feeds,
  same upstream cause as dohweb.
- **chonburi** 1/2 — Hwy 331 Nong Phai Kaeo failing; Bang Lamung (the
  Pattaya-area cam) has a last-good thumb from 07:40 and shows its
  STALE/OFFLINE status card.
- **rama9** is the only fully-healthy zone (6/6, pulled <1min ago).

## Vs. the 09-30 audit (`camera-sources-2026-09-30`)

- Worse: noble-park was partially live (swimming pool snap verified 10-01),
  now all-dead. tony-house still broken (Xiaomi token) and now ip_cam_65 is
  out too. dohweb degraded from healthy to 1/10.
- Unchanged: noble-a DVR still cloud-offline; chonburi/burapha still
  upstream-limited.

## Honesty check

Per camwall standard: nothing above is hidden — all 41 down cams keep
last-good thumbs or generated status cards, and the walls show the labelled
STALE/DELAYED/OFFLINE cards rather than blank tiles.

# CCTV Request Flow — Voice Command to Screen (Ada · VMS · XMEye)

How "Ada, show me the swimming pool camera" becomes a picture on a screen,
including the XMEye DVR layer. Written 2026-10-01 alongside the status-card
standard rollout.

## The chain

```
voice turn  →  ada_camera_snapshot {channel}
        │        backend/realtime_provider.py — 45s budget
        ▼        backend/vms_camera.py — GET mn01:8377/snap?ch=…
   vms-snap.py on mn01 (inside xmeye-vms podman, Wine + Xvfb :99)
   1. channels.json — name/alias → {x,y, device: DVR serial}
   2. global lock (serial — one snap at a time, ~35–90s worst case)
   3. xdotool: pin 4-grid → scroll device tree → double-click channel row
   4. row-highlight verification (layout-drift guard)
   5. double-click pane 1 → zoom (~4× resolution)
   6. _has_video poll — 3 rounds × 8 × 1.5s; re-select between rounds
   7. xwd -root → crop pane → PNG → 200 (+x-channel header)
   8. dead after retries → 503 · unknown name → 404 + channel list
      watchdog: 3 consecutive all-dead sweeps → restarts VMS.exe
        │
        ▼   P2P attach over XMEye cloud (www.xmeye.net)
     DVR     noble-club  serial d811d82e21d6c031
             noble-a     serial f2ca2dca0bc4ae4f…
        │
        ▼  PNG returns to Ada
   _camera_snapshot publishes the frame to the input-bridge
   (POST /api/input-bridge/frame, token=cam:<slug>-<ts>) → cast_url,
   plus a static copy under /static/cam-snap/.
   Vision sidecar (moondream @ tony-omen:11434, ADA_VISION_MODE=describe)
   turns the frame into text — no Gemini image quota burned.
        │
        ▼
   cast_to_screen(action='image', url=cast_url) → screen N
   vcast_snapshot verifies what's actually displayed.
```

## DVR realities the flow has to survive

- **Device-tree listing ≠ liveness.** A DVR can list all channels while its
  cloud session is dead (noble-a red-X for ~36h). Only a stream attach
  proves the camera is up — that's what the _has_video poll checks.
- **Serial shim.** One global lock; every snap holds it for up to ~90s.
  The camwall puller budget-skips VMS zones so walls don't starve.
- **Tree drift.** channels.json is a positional map — the shim verifies the
  selected row and errors loudly ('recalibrate channels.json') instead of
  snapping the wrong camera.

## Guaranteed-image standard (2026-10-01)

Live snap fails → `stale_snapshot()` finds the camwall last-good thumb by
slug across the VMS zone manifests → result carries `stale:true, age_s,
live_error`. A failed pull generates `<key>-status.jpg` — dimmed last-good
+ bilingual banner (STALE/DELAYED/OFFLINE/NO SIGNAL + "last frame <age>"):

| class   | trigger                        | look                         |
|---------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|
| stale   | pull failed, thumb < 6h        | dimmed frame + amber STALE   |
| delayed | VMS budget skip this cycle     | dimmed frame + blue DELAYED  |
| offline | no thumb ever, or > 6h old     | red OFFLINE (slate/dimmed)   |
| error   | other                          | NO SIGNAL                    |

Consumers: wall tiles show the card when !ok · montage bakes the card ·
**the card is what lands on a cast screen** for a dead cam — the raw
last-good still feeds the describe/vision path. Card deleted on next
successful pull. Standard: docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.camwall.yml.

## Reports → CMS → Ada tells Tony (closed loop)

- `cam-wall-cms.py` (15min timer, tony-dell) republishes `wall-<zone>` +
  `cctv-walls` index + per-zone 24h detection timeline into ada-cms-pages.
- As of 2026-10-01 it also diffs per-zone live counts
  (`_cms-notify-state.json`) and POSTs `/api/notify` on transitions only —
  zone recovered, zone went all-dead. Deferred (non-urgent) note — Ada
  relays it without hijacking the current turn.
- Ada-side rules: 'live' only for fresh snap or age < 2×interval; stale →
  quote the age; no thumb ever → 'no image yet'. wall_offline_dvr scenario
  guards the all-dead honesty path.

## Verified live 2026-10-01

camera_stale_fallback PASS (tennis, honest age) · camera_snapshot PASS
(pool, "17 min ago") · camera_snapshot_offline PASS (guardhouse,
"2,096 min ago") · wall_offline_dvr PASS (noble-a all-dead) · wall_ops
PASS · noble-a partially back: Road In + Walkway In live (visible flood
water on Road In), Guard View / Road Corner / CAM01 still OFFLINE cards.

docs.contentMd:
# สายท่อ CCTV ของอาดา — จากคำสั่งเสียงถึงภาพบนจอ

เวอร์ชันภาษาไทยของ "CCTV Request Flow" — อธิบายว่าประโยคว่า
"อาดา ขอดูกล้องสระว่ายน้ำหน่อย" กลายเป็นภาพบนจอได้ยังไง
รวมถึงชั้น XMEye DVR ด้วย (เขียน 2026-10-01)

## ลำดับขั้นตอน

```
คำสั่งเสียง  →  ada_camera_snapshot {channel}
        │        backend/realtime_provider.py — เวลาสูงสุด 45 วินาที
        ▼        backend/vms_camera.py — GET mn01:8377/snap?ch=…
   vms-snap.py บน mn01 (ใน podman xmeye-vms, Wine + Xvfb :99)
   1. channels.json — ชื่อ/alias → {x,y, device: serial ของ DVR}
   2. global lock (ทำทีละเครื่อง — snap หนึ่งใช้เวลา ~35–90 วินาที)
   3. xdotool: กริด 4 ช่อง → เลื่อน device tree → ดับเบิลคลิกแถวช่อง
   4. ตรวจว่าแถวถูกเลือกจริง (กัน layout เพี้ยน)
   5. ดับเบิลคลิก pane 1 → zoom (~4× ความละเอียด)
   6. _has_video poll — 3 รอบ × 8 × 1.5 วินาที; ลองเลือกใหม่ระหว่างรอบ
   7. xwd -root → crop pane → PNG → 200 (+header x-channel)
   8. ตายหลังลองซ้ำ → 503 · ชื่อไม่รู้จัก → 404 + รายชื่อช่อง
      watchdog: 3 รอบติดกันที่ทุกกล้องตาย → รีสตาร์ท VMS.exe
        │
        ▼   ต่อ P2P ผ่าน XMEye cloud (www.xmeye.net)
     DVR     noble-club  serial d811d82e21d6c031
             noble-a     serial f2ca2dca0bc4ae4f…
        │
        ▼  PNG กลับมาที่ Ada
   _camera_snapshot ส่งเฟรมเข้า input-bridge
   (POST /api/input-bridge/frame, token=cam:<slug>-<ts>) → cast_url,
   บวกสำเนา static ที่ /static/cam-snap/
   Vision sidecar (moondream @ tony-omen:11434, ADA_VISION_MODE=describe)
   แปลงภาพเป็นข้อความ — ไม่เสียโควต้าภาพของ Gemini
        │
        ▼
   cast_to_screen(action='image', url=cast_url) → จอหมายเลข N
   vcast_snapshot ยืนยันว่าจอแสดงจริง
```

## ความจริงของ DVR ที่ระบบต้องรอด

- **รายชื่อช่องใน device tree ≠ กล้องมีชีวิต** — DVR list ช่องครบได้ทั้งที่
  session cloud ตาย (noble-a ขึ้นกากบาทแดง ~36 ชม.) การพิสูจน์จริงคือ
  การ attach stream — นี่คือสิ่งที่ _has_video ตรวจ
- **shim ทำทีละงาน** — lock เดียว ทุก snap ถือนานถึง ~90 วินาที
  camwall puller มี budget ข้ามโซน VMS เพื่อไม่ให้ wall อื่นติด
- **tree เพี้ยนได้** — channels.json เป็นแผนที่เชิงตำแหน่ง; shim ตรวจแถวที่เลือก
  และแจ้งเตือนดัง ๆ ('recalibrate channels.json') แทนที่จะส่งภาพกล้องผิดตัว

## มาตรฐาน "มีภาพเสมอ" (2026-10-01)

ถ้า snap สดล้มเหลว → `stale_snapshot()` หาภาพล่าสุดจาก camwall manifest
→ ผลลัพธ์มี `stale:true, age_s, live_error`; เมื่อ pull ไม่สำเร็จจะสร้าง
`<key>-status.jpg` — ภาพล่าสุดแบบหรี่ + แบนเนอร์สองภาษา
(STALE/DELAYED/OFFLINE/NO SIGNAL + "เฟรมล่าสุด <อายุ>"):

| ประเภท   | เงื่อนไข                          | หน้าตา                         |
|---------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| stale   | pull พลาด แต่ thumb อายุ < 6 ชม.   | เฟรมหรี่ + แถบ STALE สีเหลือง   |
| delayed | VMS ถูกข้ามด้วย budget รอบนี้       | เฟรมหรี่ + แถบ DELAYED สีฟ้า    |
| offline | ไม่เคยมี thumb หรือเก่า > 6 ชม.     | OFFLINE แดง                    |
| error   | อื่น ๆ                             | NO SIGNAL                      |

ผู้ใช้: tile ใน wall แสดงการ์ดเมื่อ !ok · montage อบการ์ดเข้ารูป ·
**การ์ดคือสิ่งที่ขึ้นจอ cast** สำหรับกล้องตาย — ภาพดิบล่าสุดใช้กับ
describe/vision เท่านั้น · การ์ดถูกลบเมื่อ pull สำเร็จรอบถัดไป
มาตรฐาน: docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.camwall.yml

docs.contentMd:
# CCTV Venue Network Access — noble DVRs

**Status: noble-club DVR is at 192.168.1.200 on the venue LAN (router 192.168.1.1); cloud-P2P is the only path today — a Tailscale node at the venue is the fix, not router VPN.**

## Latest

- **2026-10-05** — Drove the Wine-VMS on mn01 into noble-club's remote Device Config → Network: DVR LAN 192.168.1.200 (static, DHCP off), gateway/DNS 192.168.1.1, media port 34567, HTTP 80, RTSP enabled, MAC 00:12:42:60:0a:c4.
- **2026-10-05** — UPnP disabled on the DVR (ports all 0); DDNS tab empty. No existing port-forward or public hostname for the venue.
- **2026-10-05** — Home-LAN scan for :554 found nothing; VMS log shows `login type = cloud sn`, `ip=` empty — the DVR never reports a LAN IP over the cloud relay.
- **2026-10-05** — Assessed `iEvgeny/cctv-viewer` (Qt6+ffmpeg RTSP grid): viable as a light camera-wall *only* once an RTSP endpoint is reachable; useless while DVRs are cloud-ID-only.
- **2026-10-05** — Assessed XMEye Pro for Android: not an upgrade — replaces the Wine shim with a larger Android emulator shim, same cloud path, worse automation surface for Ada.

Sections: [Current topology](#current-topology) · [Findings](#findings) · [Why router VPN is the wrong question](#why-router-vpn-is-the-wrong-question) · [Recommended path](#recommended-path) · [Tooling options once reachable](#tooling-options-once-reachable)

## Current topology

```
venue LAN (192.168.1.0/24)
  noble-club DVR  192.168.1.200  (media 34567, http 80, rtsp 554)
  noble-a DVR     (same venue, second unit — config unread yet)
        |
        | outbound only → XMEye cloud relay (xmeye.net)
        v
home: mn01 wine-vms (cloud sn login) → Xvfb/x11vnc → noVNC
        → vms-snap (xdotool+xwd) → Ada camera tools
```

## Findings

1. **Cloud-only reachability.** Both DVRs register by cloud serial ID (`d811d82e21d6c031`, `f2ca2dca0bc4ae4fnxjd`). The VMS SDK log confirms `login type = cloud sn` with an empty `ip=` field — there is no routable address from home to the DVRs.
2. **No UPnP escape.** The DVR's UPnP feature is disabled and unconfigured, so no automatic port-forward exists even if the venue router supports UPnP.
3. **No DDNS.** The DDNS tab (cpplusddns.com) is empty — the venue has no known public hostname, so its public IP/CGNAT status is unknown.
4. **DVR is fully configurable remotely.** Remote Config works over the cloud channel — network, RTSP, UPnP, DDNS tabs are all reachable. This is enough to flip UPnP or set DDNS later *if* that path is ever chosen.

## Why router VPN is the wrong question

Checking the venue router for VPN support was the original ask. Two blockers make it moot:

1. **CGNAT.** Thai ISP connections are very commonly behind carrier NAT — inbound tunnels can't reach the venue regardless of router capability.
2. **Router admin.** Even with a VPN-capable router, it needs venue-side credentials and a config change.

A **Tailscale subnet router** needs neither: any always-on device on the venue LAN (old phone, Pi, mini PC) dials *out* to the tailnet and advertises `192.168.1.0/24`. That makes `192.168.1.200:34567`/`:554` directly reachable from every home host.

## Recommended path

1. Put a Tailscale node on the venue LAN; `tailscale up --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24`.
2. Accept the route on the tailnet admin console (or via tailscale serve/exit config).
3. Verify: `curl http://192.168.1.200/` from home — DVR web UI should answer.
4. Then retire Wine-VMS to management-only: pull frames via the DVRIP protocol directly (headless), feed cctv-viewer walls, or keep VMS for config while Ada's snapshot lane goes headless.

## Tooling options once reachable

| Tool | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `alexshpilkin/dvrip` (python) | DVRIP/Sofia protocol client on :34567 | Headless snapshots/config — replaces vms-snap xdotool lane |
| `Noneawe/xmeye-nvr-tools` | CLI recon + alarm events + snapshots | Companion `ha-xmeye-nvr` HA integration exists |
| `iEvgeny/cctv-viewer` | Qt6 multi-RTSP grid wall | Light camera-wall; RTSP `user=…&password=…&channel=N&stream=0.sdp` |
| `alexpalyan/xmcam-local` | Go mock of VideoPlayTool.exe | XM camera web UI without Windows plugin |
| Wine-VMS (current) | Management + playback | Keep for DVR admin and archive playback |

## Open questions

- Venue public IP / CGNAT status — needs someone on the venue side (or the Tailscale node itself reports it).
- Is there an always-on device at the venue today? If not, cheapest option is an old Android phone running Tailscale.
- noble-a's LAN IP is still unread — same VMS Config path on `noble-a` gives it once the subnet route exists it becomes moot.

*Generated by devin · 2026-10-05Z · sources: VMS Device Config screenshots, XMConnectDeviceLog.txt, LAN :554 scan, GitHub repo review*

docs.contentMd:
# Chaba Edge Plan — Cloudflare on surf-thailand.com

_2026-09-27 · Devin · domain: chaba.surf-thailand.com + *.chaba.surf-thailand.com_

## Architecture

```
internet → Cloudflare edge (SIN, ~15ms from TH)
         → cloudflared on idc01 (outbound-only, no public inbound ports)
         → per-hostname ingress → local services
```

`cloudflared` runs as a quadlet on idc01 (second instance on idc02 later
— CF health-checks tunnel replicas natively → free failover). idc01's
firewall drops ALL public inbound once the tunnel is live; today's
public IP stops mattering except as a SSH/Tailscale backdoor.

## Hostname layout

One wildcard DNS record + explicit ingress rules (keeps the app list
audited — no accidental exposure by adding a local service):

| Hostname | Backend | Access policy |
|---|---|---|
| `chaba.surf-thailand.com` | status/landing page (static, in stacks/web) | public |
| `ada.chaba…` | ada-pi-pwa :8001 | **none** — app-level user keys (KK/guests use this) |
| `cms.chaba…` | CMS pages (ada-pwa /cms or dedicated) | Access: Tony Google login |
| `gev.chaba…` | GEV + `/apps/gev-live/ws` | Access: Tony |
| `obsidian.chaba…` | obsidian-vault | Access: Tony |
| `mddb.chaba…` | mddb-panel | Access: Tony + CF rate-limit |
| `vms.chaba…` | noVNC bridge | Access: Tony (replaces Tailscale-User-Login gating for off-tailnet use) |

Cloudflared ingress sketch:

```yaml
ingress:
  - hostname: ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:8001
  - hostname: cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:8001
    originRequest: {httpHostHeader: cms}
  - hostname: gev.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:80        # caddy serves the static bundle
  - hostname: "*.chaba.surf-thailand.com"
    service: http_status:404           # explicit deny by default
  - service: http_status:404
```

## What each CF layer buys here

- **Tunnel**: zero inbound attack surface on the VPS — upgrades the
  "tailnet-only" posture to cover public reach too. The public IP can
  eventually go (cheaper VPS tier).
- **Access**: Google's login becomes the perimeter for Tony-only apps —
  better than IP tricks and works from any network. App-level keys
  (ada PWA) stay for shared/guest apps.
- **WAF + rate limiting**: protects the Ada endpoint from quota abuse —
  a public voice agent is free Gemini/OpenRouter compute for scrapers
  otherwise.
- **Caching**: PWA/static assets at SIN edge — actual speedup for the
  iPad.

## Privacy note (the one real cost)

CF terminates TLS for every proxied/tunneled app — voice transcripts and
memory content transit their edge in plaintext internally. For a
personal stack this is usually acceptable, but sensitive paths
(mddb-panel, obsidian) could stay tailnet-only if that ever bothers us —
the tunnel layout doesn't force anything public.

## Rollout order

1. Register DNS zone in CF, set `chaba.surf-thailand.com` + `*.chaba` CNAMEs
2. `cloudflared` quadlet on idc01, token from CF Zero-Trust dashboard
3. Start with ONE hostname: `ada` — verify ws/audio work through CF
4. Layer Access policies on Tony-only apps
5. When idc02 exists: second `cloudflared` → automatic tunnel HA
6. Only then consider dropping the public IP / tightening idc01 firewall

## Setup — DNS + Cloudflare (do in this order)

### 1. Onboard the domain (one-time, ~5 min + propagation)

1. CF dashboard → **Add site** → `surf-thailand.com` → Free plan
2. CF assigns two nameservers (e.g. `x.ns.cloudflare.com`)
3. At the domain registrar: replace existing NS records with CF's pair
4. Wait for CF to show **Active** (minutes to hours; `dig NS surf-thailand.com` to check)

### 2. Create the tunnel

1. **Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create** → name `chaba` → copy the token
2. Choose **dashboard-managed** (public hostnames edited in UI — no config files on the box)

### 3. cloudflared on idc01 (quadlet)

`stacks/services/cloudflared/cloudflared.container`:

```ini
[Container]
Image=docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
Exec=tunnel --no-autoupdate run
Secret=<cf-tunnel-token-secret-name>,type=env,target=TUNNEL_TOKEN
Network=host

[Service]
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

```bash
podman secret create cf_tunnel_token < <(echo -n 'eyJ...TOKEN...')
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user start cloudflared
systemctl --user status cloudflared   # look for "Registered tunnel connection"
```

### 4. Public hostnames (dashboard — auto-creates the DNS)

For each row below, **Tunnels → chaba → Public Hostnames → Add**:

| Public hostname | Service | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:80` (caddy → status page) | public |
| `ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:8001` | none (app keys) |
| `cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:8001` (path /apps/ha/ada-tony/cms) | Tony only |
| `gev.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:80` | Tony only |
| `obsidian.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:<obsidian port>` | Tony only |
| `mddb.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:<panel port>` | Tony only |

Adding each hostname auto-creates the matching `CNAME →
<tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com` record — no manual DNS editing needed.
(Verify: **DNS → Records** will show them all, proxied.)

### 5. Access policies (Tony-only apps)

**Zero Trust → Access → Applications → Add** — one app per Tony-only
hostname, or one app covering `*.chaba.surf-thailand.com` minus the
public paths:

- Application domain: `cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com` (repeat per app)
- Policy: `Allow` → `Emails: <your gmail>` → provider: Google
- Session duration: 12h (re-login is cheap on a personal stack)

### 6. Verify

```bash
curl -sI https://ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com/ | head -3     # 200 + cf-ray header
curl -sI https://cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com/ | grep -i location  # 302 → CF login
dig +short ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com   # → <id>.cfargotunnel.com
```

Ada voice sanity: open `ada.chaba…`, one utterance — websockets pass
through the tunnel transparently.

### 7. Lock down idc01 (last step, after ~a week of clean tunnel runs)

```bash
# keep only Tailscale+SSH public; drop 80/443 inbound on the public iface
sudo ufw deny in on <pubiface> to any port 80,443 proto tcp
```

Test tailnet access before/after — the tunnel makes public inbound
unnecessary, but keep SSH on the public IP until you're confident.

docs.contentMd:
# Chaba HA Plan

_2026-09-27 · Devin · goal: survive idc01 loss without losing memory or voice_

## Current posture (what already exists)

The floor is better than it looks — three of the four HA primitives are
already running:

| Primitive | Status |
|---|---|
| Nightly mddb snapshot | ✅ `mddb-backup.timer` 02:30 → native `/v1/backup` → `~/mddb-backups/` (7-day retention) |
| Off-host backup copy | ✅ `mddb-backup-pull.timer` on tony-omen |
| Standby replica | ✅ `mddb-standby-pull.timer` on tony-dell — file-copy replica |
| Ada standby node | ✅ mn01 runs Ada standby (chaba-web lane) |
| Portable stacks | ✅ all services are host-agnostic quadlets under `stacks/services/*` |
| Readiness gates | ✅ ada-* waits for mddb `/health` (installed 2026-09-27) |
| Health visibility | ⚠️ mcp-health exists; no uptime alerting yet (Beszel proposed) |
| Verified restore | ❌ restore tested for open-notebook only (`open-notebook-restore-check.timer`); mddb restore never rehearsed |
| Live replication | ❌ file-copy standby ≠ live replica; mddb upstream HAS real replication |

## Tiering — what HA actually means here

| Tier | Services | Target |
|---|---|---|
| **A — must survive** | mddb (all Ada memory), ada-ha-tony | RPO ≤24h now → ≤5min with replication; RTO ≤30min |
| **B — degraded OK** | ada-pi-pwa, caddy-edge, obsidian-vault, open-notebook | RPO ≤24h, RTO ≤2h |
| **C — best effort** | doc-archive, mddb-panel, input-bridge, ollama-proxy | rebuild when convenient |

## The plan

### Phase 1 — make rebuild deterministic (now, no new hardware)

The recovery path is the weak link: backups exist but **restore has
never been rehearsed**. One mddb restore drill + a written runbook:

1. Restore drill: take last night's `mddb-backups/*.db`, stand it up
   on tony-dell as `mddb-restore-test`, point an Ada client at it,
   verify a memory recall. Time it — that's our real RTO.
2. Write `runbook-idc01-rebuild.md`: fresh VPS → tailscale up → clone
   chaba → install.sh per stack → restore mddb.db → enable units.
   Target: <90 min cold rebuild.
3. Extend `open-notebook-restore-check` pattern to mddb: monthly
   automated restore-verify timer (restore to scratch container,
   `/v1/stats` doc-count check, tear down).

### Phase 2 — idc02 live replica (when the second server lands)

4. **mddb real replication**: upstream `tradik/mddb` ships primary→
   replica sync (the restore-sync fixes I found earlier are in this
   path). Run idc01 primary → idc02 replica; RPO drops from 24h to
   near-zero. The file-copy standby on tony-dell stays as tier-3
   insurance.
5. **Ada failover pair**: ada-ha-tony stays primary on idc01; mn01
   standby already exists — formalize: keep mn01's Ada pointed at
   mddb on the tailnet IP (not idc01-specific), document the manual
   cutover (switch HA websocket endpoint).
6. **Edge split — revised**: public reach moves to a **Cloudflare
   Tunnel** (`chaba-edge-plan`): outbound-only `cloudflared` on idc01,
   subdomain-per-app, CF Access as the identity gate. idc01 drops all
   public inbound. On idc02 a second `cloudflared` gives CF-native
   tunnel failover — the Phase-3 automatic failover comes free and
   safe (CF health-checks the tunnel, not our apps).

### Phase 3 — automatic failover (later, optional)

7. Healthcheck-driven routing: caddy `lb_policy` + health_uri across
   mddb primaries, or Tailscale `tailscale serve` failover. Only worth
   it once Phase 2 proves the replica is trustworthy — automatic
   failover to a bad replica is worse than manual.

## Failure matrix

| Event | Impact today | Plan answer |
|---|---|---|
| mddb crash-loop | Ada can't recall; restart storms | gates (done) + restore-verified backups (P1) |
| idc01 dies entirely | everything public + voice + memory down | tony-dell file-replica + mn01 Ada standby (P1 drill proves it) |
| idc01 + slow rebuild | days of degraded ops | idc02 live replica (P2) |
| mddb db corruption | backup restores corrupted copy | 7-day retention + off-host copy (done) |

## Cost of the honest version

- Phase 1: ~2 hours of my time, zero money
- Phase 2: idc02 (~฿420–856/mo — see `hosting-provider-assessment`)
- Phase 3: skip until needed — manual cutover at this scale is fine;
  premature failover automation is its own outage generator

**Bottom line**: provider backups correctly skipped — our RPO is the
nightly snapshot + off-host pull, our RTO is an unrehearsed restore.
The next concrete action is a **restore drill**, not more backup
infrastructure.

# Chaba Lab — evaluation platform for Ada

Date: 2026-09-27 · goal: stable, repeatable evaluation KK can test for real

## What exists now (live)

- **51 live scenarios** in `ada-pi/tests/scenarios-live/` covering memory,
  CMS, cast, devin ledger, speaker-ID, docs, persona, recall.
- **`scripts/scenario-report.py`** — suite runner; writes one doc per
  scenario into `ada-ha-scenario-reports` (never pollutes memory search),
  retries once and marks `flaky`, supports per-scenario keys/device/URL.
- **`scripts/ada/lab-results.py`** — renders latest per scenario → CMS
  page `lab-results` (status matrix: pass/flaky/fail, failed turns, time).
- **`ada-scenario-smoke.timer`** on idc01 — hourly `--tier smoke` run +
  auto-rerender of `lab-results`. (Nightly full run: add `OnCalendar` for
  `--tier full` when the suite settles — full takes ~30-60 min.)
- **Real-user flows**: `kk_first_contact`, `kk_info_probe`, plus a guest
  key path — KK can be handed an iPad and walked through the checklist
  while transcripts auto-evaluate.

## For KK — lab checklist

CMS page `lab-checklist` holds a fixed set of voice tasks (ask time/
flood status, remember a preference, publish a page, ask to recall it
next session, try an English question). Each session gets a transcript;
a `transcript_eval` pass grades tool-calls, answer correctness, and
language fidelity afterward — real-user signal without scripting her.

## Roadmap

1. Smoke timer live hourly — watch `lab-results` tomorrow for flakes.
2. Nightly `--tier full` + weekly trend digest to `chaba-home/report`.
3. `speaker:` session override so KK-scoped scenarios run in CI (today
   they need her voice).
4. Coverage matrix (mn01 job running): map tools→scenario coverage,
   auto-flag uncovered verbs.
5. Bench metrics: p50/p95 turn latency + tool-call count per scenario —
   the runner already logs them; surface on `lab-results`.

## How to use it day to day

- Before touching `backend/`: run smoke tier → `lab-results` green.
- New feature = new scenario first (TDD for voice behavior).
- KK test day: checklist page + record sessions + eval pass after.

# Chaba Nest — the compound-AI system

**One umbrella name for all of it**: the swarm of micro-AIs mix-and-matched
to do what a single big model does — cheaper, auditable, and correctable.
"Cascade" is the *how* (levels chained in series/parallel/router/verifier
patterns); the Nest is the whole thing they live in.

Three organs:

- **Cognition tiers** — L0 rules (free) → L1 students (~1b) → L2 heavies
  (~4b) → L3 arbiter (Gemini). Cheapest tier that can hold the decision
  wins the call.
- **Memory spine** — MDDB banks, CMS report pages, corpus-in/corpus-out
  loops (misses become next run's cases).
- **Compute fabric** — host lanes across idc02/idc03/tony-omen + podman
  container lanes (runner-agent) + dispatch lanes + Colab burst GPU for
  training/bench spikes.

Authority standard (the part that keeps it safe): **program decides what
to do, AI decides how to say it.** Advisory models earn enforcement only
through measured benchmark wins — Jev advisory, CAM++ speaker shadow, and
kanban-act all live in shadow-first posture.

# Chaba Project

_Started 2026-09-27 by Devin — scaffold for Tony to review & expand.
Edit freely; sections marked ◦ need your input._

## What Chaba is

Chaba (ชบา) is the operator's knowledge-and-automation layer for the
whole home estate: the git repo of record, the SSOT document set, the
memory/context system, and the scripts that keep everything in sync.
It started life as a 3DGS/Frigate research stack (README still says
so — stale) and grew into the brain of the operation.

**Rule of thumb:** Ada is the voice; Chaba is the memory and the map.

## Estate naming (the Chaba family)

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| **Chaba** | this repo — SSOT, docs, scripts, vault, stacks |
| **Chaba Home** | Home Assistant estate (tony-ha, michael-ha, michael-dev) |
| **Chaba Voice** | Ada estate — ada-pi, ada-ha-*, PWA, speaker-id |
| **Chaba Core** | shared infra: mddb, embedding proxy, ollama, notebooklm, Caddy edge |
| **Chaba Lab** | isolated test/benchmark environment (planned — needs idc02) |

## Subsystems

- **SSOT** (`docs/ssot/`) — single-source YAML for hosts, services,
  HA entities/dashboards, security, schedules, focus items. Rendered
  into memory context (`render-memory.py`), validated by CI hook.
- **Ada memory vault** (`docs/ada-memory/`) — markdown banks synced to

  Devin publish; one doc per page, `kind: page`. ◦ Naming convention:
  Ada proposed `<section>-<slug>` — decide once and pin it.

  conversational tests; `lab-results` CMS page is the rendered matrix.

  embed-proxy source-of-truth (`scripts/mddb/gemini-ollama-proxy.mjs`).

# Chaba systemwide assessment

_Joint report by Ada + Devin — live collaboration run 2026-09-27. Ada contributed memory-bank findings and the plan; Devin contributed host audits, the report-registry state, and SSOT validation._

## Ada's half

From memory and current checks:

*   **Status:** System has 8 completed Devin tasks (implementing PWA Focus tab, enhanced state tracking, etc.). Home Assistant plugs are stable, but a logbook query failed. Most sensors are online, except the RK600 weather station which is reporting with no data.
*   **Issues:** Failing to read Home Assistant logic, missing sensor data from the RK600 card.
*   **Open Attention Items:** Overdue chore tasks (tap repair, PCB follow-up), Devin memory.yml proposal, missing Cache Video Report update.

## Devin's half

From live host audits and the report registry:

*   **Registry:** **ATTENTION.** 3 missing nodes (audit-suite, memory-suite, macbook audit), 6 stale nodes (all host audits [Omen, Dell, Mn01, Idc01] last ran 2026-09-25, overnight-assessment, system-report). Scheduled L2 renderers (fleet, ada-memory-report) not built; report-feed is remote-only.
*   **Validation:** SSOT is clean (691 files, 0 errors, 1 warning).
*   **Hosts:** Confirmed expected services are present, but with failed units:
    *   **tony-dell:** xiaomi-token-refresh failing (fix: Chrome re-login to account.xiaomi.com), xdg portal units.
    *   **tony-omen:** nvidia-cdi-refresh (needs pending reboot for NVML mismatch), michael-dev-parity, arp-inventory-scan.
    *   **idc01:** ada-scenario-smoke failing, ada-memory-sync failing on push conflicts after migration. (idc01 rebooted 20:42 during this assessment; MDDB + Ada recovered.)
    *   **mn01:** portal noise, grub-initrd-fallback.
    *   **kk-macbook:** Offline and unaudited.
*   **Attention:** Focus inbox has 139 unprocessed files again.

## Joint Prioritized Action Plan

1.  Investigate failed logbook queries.
2.  Fix failed system units:
    *   Reboot tony-omen (Nvidia driver).
    *   Relogin on tony-dell (Xiaomi token).
    *   Fix git conflicts on idc01 (memory sync).
3.  Process Focus inbox.
4.  Investigate RK600 weather station failure.
5.  Resolve registry attention state (missing/stale nodes; build fleet + ada-memory-report renderers; install chaba-system-report.timer).
6.  Address overdue chores and memory.yml proposal.

## Follow-ups found during this run (root-caused 2026-09-27/10-03)

*   `cms_publish_page` → MDDB `/v1/add` 404 was **mddb OOM crash churn**, not a transient: idc01`s mddb was OOM-killed 4x in ~40 min (19:50-20:27). During each ~1-min warmup `/health` answers but `/v1` routes are not yet registered — the publish landed in that window. Every restart also triggered a full binlog resync from LSN=0 to the tony-dell read-only follower (~12 GiB RSS spike, settling ~3 GiB). Filed: `docs/ssot/focus-inbox/finding-2026-09-27-idc01-mddb-oom-loop.yml` (MemoryMax, follower LSN persistence, OOM alerting, 2.15.3 upgrade).
*   Logbook failure was a post-reboot transient — `/api/home-assistant/logbook` returns `connected` again.
*   RK600 "no data" is a **real gap**, not a bug: RK600 entities live on michael-ha; ada-ha-tony queries tony-ha only — the approved `mha_mirror_*` mirror package was never deployed.
*   idc01 rebooted mid-run (clean shutdown 20:42); Ada, mddb and the replication follower all recovered.

subject: cms-edit-manual
summary: How to use the CMS Edit drawer: add/update/improve/expand/consolidate/split/merge on pages and ## sections; ops semantics + what auto-updates on every edit.
title: CMS Edit Manual

docs.contentMd:
# CMS Edit Manual — how to work on pages

The CMS viewer now has an **Edit drawer**: open any page, click **Edit**
(top-right), pick a section (or "whole page"), and push a button.

## The ops

| op | what it does | needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Add** | appends markdown to the page (or into a section) | text |
| **Update** | replaces the section body, or the whole page if no section picked | text |
| **Improve** | rewrites tighter — keeps every fact, no new info | section (or page) |
| **Expand** | deepens the section with more detail | section (or page) |
| **Consolidate** | merges overlapping/duplicate sections in a page | page |
| **Split →** | moves the picked section to a NEW page, leaves a link behind | section + target slug |
| **Merge ←** | pulls another page's content into this one and marks that page superseded | target slug |

## Sections

Sections are markdown `## Heading` blocks — pick one by name from the
dropdown. The textarea scopes to that section so you can see/edit just
it. "whole page" = the entire markdown.

## What happens on every edit

- `meta.updated` refreshes, a timeline entry is appended
- `reports-index` regenerates, so the change shows up in Ada's index
- `split`/`merge` write the `links`/`supersedes`/`superseded_by` fields
  on both pages so the graph stays honest

## Voice path is unchanged

Ada still uses `cms_publish_page` / `cms_note_update` — the drawer is a
*human* tool, not a voice tool. Voice write-confirmation gates are
untouched.

subject: cms-page-standard
title: CMS page standard — landing-page format

docs.contentMd:
# CMS page standard — landing-page format

Every `ada-cms-pages` document should open like a mini landing page:
the reader gets the verdict and the newest developments without
scrolling, and can jump to detail via section links.

## Required structure

```markdown
# Title — matches meta.title

**Status: one-line verdict a reader can act on.**

## Latest

- **YYYY-MM-DD** — newest development first, one line each (≤5 entries;
  roll older ones into a History/archive section at the bottom).

Sections: [Section A](#section-a) · [Section B](#section-b)

## Section A / Section B ...

## History — earlier dated entries, newest first (optional)

*Generated by <writer> · <date>Z · sources: <n>*  ← provenance footer
```

## Rules

1. **Status line first** — bold, immediately under the H1. Answers
   "what's the current state?" in one sentence.
2. **`## Latest` before detail** — reverse-chronological, dated bullets.
   Updated pages put the change here, not buried mid-document.
3. **Section links** — one line of markdown anchor links right after
   Latest when the page has >2 sections.
4. **Media welcome** — charts/diagrams embedded as `![alt](url)` with
   assets served from `stacks/web/public/apps/reports/` (reachable at
   `https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/reports/<file>`).
   Benchmarks should always include a graph, not just a table.
5. **Provenance footer** — `*Generated by … · sources: …*` (audit rule
   R2); generated reports also need `meta.sources` (R1).
6. **Meta** — full schema block: kind=page, slug, title, format,
   updated, bank, scope, status, source, written_by, subject,
   attribute, valid_from, last_verified.

## Audit

`scripts/ada/cms-audit.py` enforces the older A/R/N/S rules plus:
- `status: stub` or `status: archived` skips the A1 thin check — mark
  intentional stubs instead of leaving empty pages failing.
- `A5_EXEMPT` covers docs that describe the placeholder rule itself
  (`cms-audit-report`, `document-audit-policy`).

State after 2026-10-01 cleanup: **133 pass · 0 fail · 29 warnings**
(remaining warnings: S1 schema gaps on `wall-*`, C1 duplicate pairs,
R5 missing registry docs).

subject: colab-assessment
title: Colab assessment — GPU offload for chaba/ada

docs.contentMd:
# Colab Assessment — GPU offload options for the chaba/ada stack

_2026-09-27 · devin session · status: assessment (no purchase made)_

## Why now

Our only GPU host is **tony-omen** (GTX 1650 Mobile, 4 GB VRAM) — and its link
is currently down. Everything GPU-side is contended: `mcp-gpu` literally has to
`hold_llama` (drop llama-server to CPU) to free VRAM for an imagen2 run. Any
batch GPU work we add (embedding backfills, evals, transcription) competes with
the always-on Llama router. Question: can Colab absorb the batch tier?

## What Colab offers (Sept 2026)

Colab Pro/Pro+ are being folded into **Google AI plans** (announced 2026-09-22);
legacy Colab subs still work and stack.

| Tier | Price | Compute units | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | ~nothing guaranteed | T4 when available, ~12h sessions |
| **Colab Pro** | ~$9.99/mo ($8.33 annual) | 100/mo | premium GPU queue (L4/A100), high-mem machines, terminal |
| **Colab Pro+** | ~$49.99/mo ($41.66 annual) | 500/mo | Pro + **background execution** (runs without browser open) |
| Google AI Pro/Ultra | existing subs | included benefits | Ultra adds Premium GPU + uninterrupted background exec |

Rough unit burn: T4 ≈ 2 CU/hr · L4 ≈ 5 CU/hr · A100 ≈ 13 CU/hr.
So Pro ≈ ~50h T4 or ~7h A100 per month; Pro+ is 5× that.

## Fit against our workloads

| Workload | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| MDDB re-embed / embedding backfill | ✅ excellent | pure batch; nomic-embed-text or text-embedding-004 parity check, measure tokens/s vs tony-omen CPU |
| Model evals for Llama router candidates | ✅ excellent | run candidates on L4/A100, benchmark, pick — noVRAM juggling at home |
| Whisper batch transcription (audio backlogs) | ✅ excellent | large-v3 on T4 ≈ 10-20× realtime |
| Image generation batches | ✅ good | SDXL/Diffusers on L4; frees tony-omen entirely |
| LoRA fine-tunes | ⚠️ possible | fits L4/A100 but session caps bite; needs Pro+ background exec for real runs |
| Always-on services (mcp-llama, mcp-gpu) | ❌ no | ephemeral runtimes, ~24h max, idle disconnect, no inbound ports, no Docker |
| Latency-sensitive / MCP-callable compute | ❌ no | cold-start + queue; nothing to call synchronously |

**Rule of thumb: Colab = batch GPU, not a host.** Anything with a service
endpoint stays at home (or moves to a real GPU VPS).

## Alternatives compared

| Option | Cost | vs Colab |
|---|---|---|
| **Kaggle notebooks** | free, ~30 GPU-hr/wk (T4×2 / P100) | covers most of our batch needs at $0 — try this first |
| Colab Enterprise (GCP) | pay-go: T4 ~$0.49/hr, L4 ~$0.78/hr, A100 ~$4.1/hr | same notebook UX, real billing, no monthly quota cliff; better for occasional spikes |
| vast.ai / runpod | ~$0.20–0.50/hr real GPUs | can host *services* (inbound ports, Docker) — the answer if we ever need an always-on GPU endpoint |
| Google AI Ultra | existing sub check | if already subscribed, Colab premium + background exec come free — verify before buying Pro+ |

## Integration path (if adopted)

1. Keep notebook templates in repo (`notebooks/colab/` in chaba or ada-pi):
   param cell for job type + input refs; Drive folder as the artifact sink.
2. Results write-back: either (a) notebook pushes to MDDB `/v1/add` via
   userspace Tailscale (`tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking` works in Colab —
   auth key needed), or (b) write artifacts to Drive and let an idc01 cron pull.
   Option (b) is simpler and keeps secrets off the notebook.
3. Devin workflow: generate/refresh notebook → Tony kicks the run (Colab has no
   API to start runtimes unattended) → artifacts land → idc01 ingest job.

## Recommendation

- **Pilot free first**: run one MDDB re-embed benchmark on Kaggle's free
  T4×2 vs tony-omen CPU to get real numbers — no spend.
- If batch GPU becomes a recurring need: **Colab Pro at ~$10/mo** is trivially
  cheap; skip Pro+ unless overnight unattended runs matter (or it's already
  covered by an existing Google AI sub).
- If we ever need a *hosted* GPU service (always-on inference off tony-omen):
  that's vast.ai/runpod/GPU VPS territory, not Colab.

## Open questions

- Is there an existing Google AI Pro/Ultra subscription on the account?
  (If yes, most of this is already unlocked.)
- How much batch work actually exists — real backlog vs hypothetical?
- Worth a notebook template + Drive sink setup only if the pilot shows
  meaningful speedup.

subject: colab-gpu-results
title: Colab GPU Media-Gen Research

docs.contentMd:
# Colab GPU Media-Gen Research

Free Google Colab GPU (Tesla T4) as an on-demand lab for image/video generation experiments. Sessions are ephemeral — `colab run` allocates a fresh VM per job and releases it; nothing stays warm (free GPU quota is scarce and idle VMs burn it).

## Tooling

- `google-colab-cli` — provision CPU/GPU/TPU sessions from the terminal. Note: installed 0.6.0 `exec` is broken with current `jupyter-kernel-client`; pin `uvx --from google-colab-cli==0.7.4` until the venv is upgraded.
- `colab-mcp` server (uvx `git+https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp`) — registered in `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` as `colab-mcp`. Browser-side notebook control (open connection → add/run/update/move/delete/get cells).
- Experiment runner: `scripts/colab/img_gen.py` (chaba repo) — parameterized model/prompt/size/steps/seed, writes PNG + `report.json` to `/content/output`, pull with `colab download`.
- Artifacts land in `~/.local/colab-research/<exp>/` on tony-omen. Canonical notes: `docs/kb/colab-gpu-research.md` (chaba repo).

## Experiment log

### exp-01 — SD baseline (2026-09-30)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | prompthero/openjourney |
| Prompt | a serene lake in the mountains at sunset, highly detailed |
| Config | 512×512, 25 steps, guidance 7.5, seed 42 |
| Device | Tesla T4 (15360 MiB) |
| Pipeline load | 119.4 s (cold — weights download) |
| Generation time | 5.2 s |
| Peak VRAM | 3257.6 MB |
| Output | ~/.local/colab-research/exp-01/generated.png |

Result: PASS. fp16 512×512 gen is cheap on T4 — ~5 s/img, 3.2 GB VRAM. Headroom for 768×768 and for multiple images per session.

## Queue

| # | Task | Model | Config | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp-02 | Resolution scaling | prompthero/openjourney | 768×768, 25 steps | queued |
| exp-03 | Larger model | stabilityai/sdxl-turbo | 512×512 | queued — gated, needs HF_TOKEN |
| exp-04 | Video probe | SVD/Wan-class | short clip | queued — T4 feasibility check first |

## Notes

- HF downloads are unauthenticated by default (no token set). Gated models need `HF_TOKEN` in Colab secrets or `colab run --env HF_TOKEN=...`.
- Free T4 lifecycle: provision ~30–60 s, idle-timeout ~90 min, session TTL ~12 h. Plan = allocate just-in-time.
- The `colab-mcp` browser path attaches to whichever notebook is on GPU runtime — switch the runtime to GPU in the Colab UI before driving it via MCP.

# Deep-dive session flow — analysis, improvements, benchmark

Date: 2026-09-27 · scenario: `tests/scenarios-live/deep_dive_flood_report.yaml`

## What the flow should be

Discuss → drill → analyze → improve → benchmark. Tony picks an artifact
(a flood report page), talks it over with Ada, she critiques, improves it,
and re-verifies — all inside one conversation.

## Live run findings (2026-09-27)

| Turn | Expectation | Ada did | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "pull up the flood report" | `cms_get_page`/list/search | fetched + summarized correctly | ✓ |
| "analyze it like an editor" | (was: must call tool) | answered inline — no call, and the critique was genuinely good (imprecision, staleness) | ✓ behavior — scenario was wrong |
| "improve it — restructure + save + verify" | `cms_publish_page` | reached for `web_search` first, hit the 20/day grounding quota, then asked permission instead of publishing | partial |
| "yes, go ahead" | publish + verify | drafted new structure; publish handshake fired ("jumped the gun" → pending) | handshake working |

### Issues surfaced

1. **Quota trap**: when asked to *improve* a page she defaulted to
   fetching fresher data (`web_search`) instead of restructuring what
   exists — and hit the free-tier cap. Improve-with-what-we-have should
   be the default; research is a separate ask.
2. **Editorial turns shouldn't tool-call** — once the page is fetched,
   analysis is in-context. Fixed the scenario to assert `no_calls_except`
   (the L0-index design already predicted this).
3. **No benchmark turn yet** — the scenario needs a 5th step: "how do we
   measure if the report got better" → she should propose metrics
   (freshness, coverage, cite count, structure completeness) and ideally
   score the page.

## Improvements to land

- Ada instruction: "improve a page = restructure existing content; only
  reach for web_search when the user asks for new information"
- `cms_verify_page` block-report already returns structure — extend the
  improvement turn to compare before/after (report diff)
- Add a `benchmark` turn: she rates the updated page on a rubric
  (freshness/specificity/sources/structure 0-2 each) — gives a numeric
  before/after we can track in the ledger

## Benchmark proposal (report quality score)

Per report/page, score 0–8: specificity (proper names/dates), freshness
(timestamps within window), sources cited, structure completeness. Store
score in the page meta on each update — `cms_verify_page` could emit it.
Then "dig deep → improve" sessions become measurable: score should rise
each pass, and the trend is reviewable in the CMS report list.

subject: document-audit-policy
title: Document Audit Policy Report

docs.contentMd:
# Document Audit Policy Report

_2026-09-27 · Devin · live-verified against ada-cms-pages (40 pages)_

## Why this exists

Ada generates CMS pages through `cms_publish_page`, and until today
there was **no quality gate** — the first news-* batch shipped with
missing H1s, no source links, no "why it matters", and nobody could
tell without eyeballing every page. An audit rule-set now exists
(`chaba/scripts/ada/cms-audit.py`, committed `9f9eadb4`) plus a
tightened format spec (`news-system` page).

## The policy — what a page must satisfy

### Generic rules (all `kind: page` docs)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| A1 | Body non-empty, ≥ 200 chars — *the empty-shell bug (`content_md` vs `contentMd`) is exactly what this catches* |
| A2 | Meta complete: `slug`, `title`, `format`, `updated`, `kind=page` |
| A3 | H1 heading present and matching the page title |
| A4 | Real structure — headings or lists, not a bare paragraph blob |
| A5 | No placeholders (TODO / TBD / lorem / placeholder) |
| A6 | No secret-shaped strings (`api_key=`, `password:`, …) |

### News brief rules (`news-*` pages only)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| N1 | `TL;DR:` line — one sentence, concrete |
| N2 | ≤ 6 items per page |
| N3 | `[Source](url)` link per item |
| N4 | `Why it matters:` per item |

The full contract lives on the `news-system` page — Ada reads it before
drafting, so tightening the spec is the lever that improves output.

## What the first audit found (before → after)

| Group | Result |
|---|---|
| All 40 pages | 34 pass / **11 fail** |
| news-* (6 pages) | **all 6 failed**: missing H1 ×4, no sources ×4, no why-it-matters ×3, no TL;DR ×1 |

Fix loop that ran today:
1. `news_pages_update` scenario — Ada updated all 5 news pages (PASS
   on handshake/flow, but content failed audit).
2. Spec tightened → `news-system` now lists *required* elements.
3. `news_audit_fix` scenario — Ada re-drafted under the spec; 3 pages
   landed compliant, `news-world` got eaten by the pending-confirm
   handshake (she believed it published — it didn't), `news-thailand`
   was outside the fix scope.
4. Direct repair on the stragglers → **final audit: 6/6 news pass,
   37/40 overall** (remaining fails: `todo-list`, `idea-summary`,
   `cached-videos-report`, `vcast-failure-report`, `devin-job-report-fail`
   — mostly old/placeholder pages, deliberately left).

## Findings worth keeping

- **Pending-confirm can swallow a publish silently** — Ada thinks it
  landed; verify-after-publish should be mandatory, not optional
  (news-system now says so).
- **Ada invents structure per session** unless the spec is hard.
  "House style" as prose → soft compliance; as numbered MUSTs → she
  hit it on the first retry for 3/4 pages.
- **The audit is runnable cheaply** — `python3 scripts/ada/cms-audit.py
  [prefix]`, ~1s against mddb. Hookable into the scenario runner's
  ExecStopPost alongside lab-results.

## GitHub knowledge applied

- **errata-ai/vale** + `elastic/vale-rules` — the prose-linter model:
  our A-rules are a lighter, zero-dependency version (Vale itself is
  overkill for a 40-page CMS but is the upgrade path if the corpus
  grows).
- **GitHub Docs content linter** (markdownlint-based, custom rules on
  top) — the pattern we copied: stock rules *plus* collection-specific
  rules (N-rules), warning vs error severity.
- **lychee** (link checking) — not implemented yet; N3 checks link
  *presence*, a future pass could check link *liveness*.
- Microsoft code-with playbook / docs-as-code practice — "docs get the
  same gates as code" is the framing: audit on publish, not on review.

## Suggested next steps

1. Wire `cms-audit.py` into `ada-scenario-smoke`'s ExecStopPost (next to
   lab-results.py) so every suite run re-audits.
2. Add a `cms_audit` tool for Ada — she could self-check before asking
   you to confirm a publish.
3. Extend rules: image/link liveness, stale-date warnings on living
   pages (todo-list class), Thai-language pages pass fine today but a
   bilingual style rule may be worth pinning.

# รายงานการวิเคราะห์อารมณ์และพฤติกรรม

## การวิเคราะห์อารมณ์จากน้ำเสียง (Speech Emotion Recognition)
พบว่ามีงานวิจัยและโมเดลที่น่าสนใจ เช่น โมเดลจำแนกอารมณ์จากเสียงพูดภาษาไทย พัฒนาโดยอาจารย์จากจุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย

## การตรวจจับอารมณ์จากใบหน้า (Facial Emotion Recognition)
มีเทคโนโลยีตรวจจับอารมณ์จากใบหน้าผ่านกล้อง (Facial Emotion Recognition) ซึ่งสามารถนำมาใช้งานร่วมกับการวิเคราะห์เสียงเพื่อความแม่นยำที่มากขึ้น

## การจับตำแหน่งสายตา (Eye Tracking)
เจอไลบรารีที่น่าสนใจใน GitHub/GitLab ชื่อ GazeTracking สำหรับจับตำแหน่งสายตาและการมอง

## การอ่านปากจากวิดีโอ (Lip Reading)
มีโอเพนซอร์สใน GitHub เช่น LIP READING-AI สำหรับการพัฒนาระบบอ่านปากจากวิดีโอ

## ลิงก์ที่เกี่ยวข้อง
- [ปัญญาประดิษฐ์อ่านน้ำเสียงคนได้แล้ว](https://www.chula.ac.th/highlight/47227/)

docs.contentMd: # Project Analysis: V-Cast Interface & Automation Failures **Target:** Devin coding session & Ada RCA study. ## Problem Statement Ongoing issues impact user confidence in the WeCast system and automated home controls. ## Known Failures 1. ### Visual Failures (V-Cast) - Screen 1 ownership logic prevents public access. - Content fails to render (broken image icon). 2. ### Automation Loop Failures - Unexpected TV plug activation triggers. ## Devin Action Plan - [x] Analyze `chaba` PWA receiver logic for broken image handling. — DONE 2026-09-28 - [ ] Review Home Assistant logbook for plug trigger source context. --- ## Repair Outcome — 2026-09-28 (Devin dispatch, chaba) **Broken image icon — root causes found & fixed:** 1. **Scheme**: the casted URL used `http://` on `:8123`, an HTTPS-only listener (plain HTTP → bare 400). On the HTTPS receiver page it was also mixed-content blocked. Fixed: receiver's `mediaUrl()` upgrades `http:`→`https:` media URLs. 2. **Missing file**: `/local/documents/A-68/...jpg` 404s even over HTTPS on both HA instances — that path was never published (A-68 pages live only in the idc01 doc-archive, behind `X-API-Key`, unusable as ``). 3. Image load failures now surface: HUD "image failed" + toast + `state:error` to the relay (previously a silent broken icon). **"Ada can't see the cast screen" — fixed:** - Snapshot path (`snap-request` → canvas → `/frame` → `vcast_snapshot`) was live but died on cross-origin `` (tainted canvas SecurityError). New relay endpoint `GET /img?url=` (tailnet/LAN allowlisted) lets the display refetch the URL server-side so pixels stay readable. Live-verified: casting the HA cam jpg to screen 2 now returns a real 424×240 JPEG frame. - Webpage (`nav`) casts verified working on screen 2; cross-origin iframes honestly report `uncapturable-iframe` + page URL — Ada can name the page, can't screenshot it (browser security, not a bug). **Deployed:** receiver `index.html` → live web mount; `server.mjs` → idc01 `input-bridge` (restarted). iPad (screen 1) picks up the new build on next connect. **Still open:** - Screen-1 owner-lock complaint (public screen treated as private) — separate ada-pi `cast-screens.json` ACL issue, not addressed here. - `/local/documents/` publishing decision (options logged in chaba job record `2026-09-28-vcast-image-mixed-content`). - TV plug automation trigger — not investigated.
