# Google Flood Hub — Assessment & Integration Report

*Assessment of Google's Flood Hub service and how it fits our flood-monitoring stack. Canonical document lives in the chaba repo — this page is a dated mirror.*

Status: **living document** — canonical source: `chaba/docs/assessments/flood-hub-assessment.md` (git history = versions).
Rendered to CMS: 2026-10-03 · Doc last updated: 2026-09-30

## TL;DR

The shared link is Flood Hub centered on **Ongkharak district, Nakhon Nayok** (14.0893°N, 101.0840°E) — one of the three districts currently being hit by runoff released from Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam (active crisis since ~Sep 27; 300+ people in shelters, Ban Na / Pak Phli / Ongkharak downstream watch).

Flood Hub itself is **worth integrating**: free, CC BY 4.0, daily-updated 7-day riverine forecasts with a proper REST API (`floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1`). The catch: API access is **waitlist-gated** (reported wait: months). Natural fit with our stack — and we already have the delivery machinery: the `flood-report` CMS pages auto-regenerate from news feeds via `flood-news-update.py`, so Flood Hub gauge data can slot in as a second managed block once we have a key.

## What the link points at

- Center: 14.0893°N, 101.0840°E, zoom ~7.8 → Bang Sombun area, **Ongkharak district, Nakhon Nayok province** (TH-26), on the Nakhon Nayok River basin.
- Shared via Facebook (`fbclid`), almost certainly because of the **current flood event**: Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam discharge + runoff from Namtok Nang Rong / Khlong Maduea. As of Sep 29 the situation was still critical downstream. The site is JS-rendered so gauge IDs at that exact point can't be resolved without the API (see below).

## Current state in our stack (checked 2026-09-30)

Flood coverage already exists in **ada-cms**, but it's *news digests*, not Flood Hub data:

- **`flood-report`** (CMS rollup, "สถานการณ์น้ำท่วมล่าสุด") — auto-regenerated hourly by `flood-news-update.py`; feeds: `bangphli`, `samutprakan`, `bangkok-th`, `bangkok-en` (Google News RSS). Has `children: [flood-report-nongdon]`.
- **`flood-report-nongdon`** — leaf page covering Saraburi/Lopburi/Chao Phraya dam feeds. **Collapsed 2026-09-30**: was a single-child rollup of `flood-report-nongdon-saraburi` (identical feeds) — redundant layer removed; now `flood-report` → `flood-report-nongdon` (leaf) directly.
- Generator: `scripts/ada/flood-news-update.py` + `scripts/ada/flood-news-feeds.json` (chaba repo). Pages use `<!-- flood-news:auto -->` managed blocks — a clean insertion point for a second managed section with gauge data.
- Registry: `ada-cms-automation` MDDB collection — each generated page has a config doc (`run_now` flag → worker regenerates; `POST /api/cms/pages/{slug}/regenerate` triggers it). **Gotcha**: the registry doc caches its own effective config and *wins over* feeds.json — collapsing/splitting a page requires updating BOTH feeds.json and the registry doc, plus the page doc's meta.
- Nothing in ada-cms currently uses Flood Hub / gauge data — the Flood Hub assessment lives only in the repo doc (this page mirrors it).

## Service assessment

### What it is

- Google Research product (`sites.research.google/floods`, aka g.co/floodhub). Two AI models: a **hydrologic LSTM** (Nearing et al., *Nature* 627, 2024 — the operational model) forecasting river discharge, and an **inundation model** estimating affected area + depth.
- Riverine flood forecasts **up to 7 days out**, refreshed **daily**, covering **150+ countries / ~2B people** per current marketing (Bellingcat's June-2025 snapshot said 80+ countries, 1,800+ high-confidence sites, 460M people — coverage expanded since).
- Map shows color-coded gauge pins (normal → warning → danger → extreme), per-gauge hydrograph vs. thresholds, inundation layers, inundation history, basin view. Alerts also surface in Google Search/Maps/Android notifications.
- Gauge types: **real gauges** (agency data, e.g. GRDC) and **virtual HYBAS gauges** (`hybas_<id>`, HydroBASINS river reaches — most of Thailand's coverage is likely these). Each has `qualityVerified` (model meets Google's eval bar) and `hasModel` flags; UI defaults to verified only, "expert mode" shows lower-confidence gauges.
- Fully free, data is **CC BY 4.0**, no account needed to view. Thai-language UI exists (cities.google/intl/th_ALL/flood-hub).

### Limitations (honest list)

- **Riverine only.** The Bang Phli / Thepharak Rd flooding our `flood-report` tracks is urban drainage/pluvial — Flood Hub gauges may show nothing there. (The API does expose `flashFloods:search` and `significantEvents:search`, which partially covers this — needs testing once we have a key.)
- Forecasts are **approximate** — the site itself says "for informational purposes only, check official sources" (= RID/thaiwater.net/DDPM for us). Cross-checking is mandatory for alerts we act on.
- Virtual gauges without `qualityVerified` can be materially wrong; treat as advisory.
- Daily cadence — not a real-time sensor. Fine for 1–7-day outlook, useless for minute-level dam-discharge events.
- API is waitlist-gated. Flood Hub's own UI key is embedded client-side (the TAK-NZ ETL project documents that the UI calls the same public `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` endpoints), but the sanctioned path is the waitlist — use that, not their key.

## Programmatic access

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `https://floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1` (REST, API-key auth, no OAuth) |
| Access | Waitlist form → approval email → reply with Google Cloud Project ID → enable `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` |
| Cost/license | Free, CC BY 4.0 |
| Key methods | `gauges:searchGaugesByArea` (region code `TH` or polygon loop), `floodStatus:queryLatestFloodStatusByGaugeIds`, `floodStatus:searchLatestFloodStatusByArea`, `gauges:queryGaugeForecasts` (8-day daily values), `gaugeModels:batchGet` (warning/danger/extreme thresholds), `flashFloods:search`, `significantEvents:search`, `serializedPolygons/{id}` (KML inundation polygons) |
| Historical | **Inundation History** 1999–2020 (`gs://flood-forecasting/inundation_history`), **GRRR** runoff reanalysis/reforecast 1980–2023 (Colab-linked dataset) |
| Verify | Google publishes a Colab notebook to test a key |
| Caveat | HydroBASINS catchment polygons are NOT in the API (TAK-NZ confirmed); `serializedPolygons` only covers flood/inundation areas |

Existing consumers worth copying: **TAK-NZ/etl-floodhub** (poll → CoT map points, poll cadence ~120s), **Deltares DELFT-FEWS** `GoogleFloodHubV1GaugeForecast` import (request pattern: `queryGaugeForecasts?gaugeIds=...&issueTimeStart=T0-25h`, batch ≤500 gauges), **floodops** (Python connector mirroring Google's colab).

## Integration plan

Ranked by effort/benefit. All assume waitlist approval except #1.

1. **Sign up for the waitlist now** (zero code). We already have GCP projects (gev-gemini/Gemini API) — pick one, submit the form with a "home automation + local alerting" use case. Approval reportedly takes months; queue it.
2. **HA REST sensors on michael-dev** (once keyed): `gauges:searchGaugesByArea` once to enumerate Thai gauges near us (Chao Phraya basin for Bang Phli-side relevance + Nakhon Nayok basin for the current event + Saraburi/Lopburi for the nongdon pages), then poll `floodStatus:queryLatestFloodStatusByGaugeIds` every ~6–12h. Store gauge IDs + thresholds in SSOT. Follow the `mha_mirror_*`/package pattern, not ad-hoc YAML.
3. **Extend `flood-news-update.py`** — instead of a new job, add a `<!-- flood-hub:auto -->` managed block to `flood-report` + nongdon pages: today's gauge severities + 7-day trend per watched basin, next to the news digest. The regeneration plumbing (automation registry, `run_now`, worker) is already built.
4. **Ada alert path**: `flood_status` tool in ada-pi reading HA entities or hitting the API from idc01; severity ≥ WARNING → LINE push via Yomi + spoken note. Scenario test under `tests/scenarios-live/` (fits the existing `deep_dive_flood_report`/`flood_situation` family).
5. **GEV overlay**: `serializedPolygons/{id}` returns KML inundation areas — Cesium in gods-eye-view can drape these. Medium effort; only worthwhile while there's an active event or as an optional layer.
6. **Display/vcast banner**: watched gauge ≥ WARNING → banner on vcast displays / CCTV wall. Cheap once #2 exists.
7. **Cross-source sanity**: pair Flood Hub with thaiwater.net (HII) / RID so Ada can say "Google says X, RID gauge says Y" — matches the verify-before-alarming duty.

## Ways to contribute

- **Feedback/bugs**: in-site "Send feedback", plus dedicated bug and feedback forms. Pilot participants can request a meeting with the team — a genuine channel; they explicitly invite it.
- **Data**: Google's stated bottleneck is public discharge records. Channels: `floodforecasting@google.com` (help publishing data) and the **Caravan** open streamflow dataset (how hydromet agencies contribute; WMO/GRDC feed 25 countries through it). **Thailand is not currently a Caravan contributor** — if we have contacts at RID/HII, advocating Thai gauge data into Caravan is the highest-impact contribution available; it would directly improve Flood Hub accuracy for the rivers flooding right now.
- **Open-source**: no Home Assistant Flood Hub integration exists (only TAK/DELFT-FEWS/floodops). Publishing our REST-sensor config or a small HACS component would be a real contribution — CC BY 4.0 permits it.
- **Ground truth**: XMEye CCTV wall (noble-club / noble-a DVRs) + observations already compiled could validate predictions-vs-reality locally; anomalies are exactly what the bug form / pilot meetings want.

## Next actions

1. ~~Submit the waitlist form~~ — **done 2026-09-30**. Now: watch for the approval email (reportedly months).
2. On approval email: reply with Google Cloud Project ID **`flood-watch-510211`** (created 2026-09-30) → enable `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` → create key restricted to the API + idc01 IP (`157.85.110.99`) → store `FLOODS_API_KEY` in `~/.config/secrets/flood-forecasting.env`.

# Google Flood Hub — รายงานประเมินและแผนผสานระบบ

*ประเมินบริการ Flood Hub ของ Google และความเข้ากันกับระบบเฝ้าระวังน้ำท่วมของเรา เอกสารต้นฉบับอยู่ใน repo chaba — หน้านี้เป็นสำเนา ณ วันที่*

สถานะ: **เอกสารมีชีวิต** — ต้นฉบับ: `chaba/docs/assessments/flood-hub-assessment.md` (git history คือประวัติเวอร์ชัน)
render ลง CMS: 2026-10-03 · เอกสารอัปเดตล่าสุด: 2026-09-30

## สรุปย่อ

ลิงก์ที่แชร์มาคือ Flood Hub ที่โฟกัส **อำเภอองครักษ์ จังหวัดนครนายก** (14.0893°N, 101.0840°E) — หนึ่งในสามอำเภอที่กำลังรับน้ำจากการระบายของเขื่อนขุนด่านปราการชล (วิกฤตตั้งแต่ ~27 ก.ย.; คนกว่า 300 คนอยู่ในศูนย์พักพิง; เฝ้าระวัง บ้านนา / ปากพลี / องครักษ์ ตอนล่าง)

ตัว Flood Hub เอง **น่าเอาเข้าระบบ**: ฟรี, ลิขสิทธิ์ CC BY 4.0, พยากรณ์น้ำในแม่น้ำล่วงหน้า 7 วันอัปเดตรายวัน พร้อม REST API จริง (`floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1`) ปัญหาคือ API ต้อง**รอคิว waitlist** (รายงานว่ารอเป็นเดือน) เข้ากับสแต็กเราได้ดี — เครื่องจักรส่งข้อมูลมีพร้อมแล้ว: หน้า `flood-report` ใน CMS รีเจนอัตโนมัติจากฟีดข่าวผ่าน `flood-news-update.py` ดังนั้นข้อมูลเกจ Flood Hub จะเสียบเป็น managed block ที่สองได้ทันทีเมื่อมี key

## ลิงก์ชี้ไปที่ไหน

- ศูนย์กลาง: 14.0893°N, 101.0840°E zoom ~7.8 → บริเวณบางสมบูรณ์ **อำเภอองครักษ์ จ.นครนายก** (TH-26) บนลุ่มน้ำนครนายก
- แชร์ผ่าน Facebook (`fbclid`) แทบแน่ใจว่าเพราะ **เหตุน้ำท่วมปัจจุบัน**: การระบายน้ำเขื่อนขุนด่านฯ + น้ำไหลจากน้ำตกนางรอง / คลองมะเดื่อ ณ 29 ก.ย. สถานการณ์ตอนล่างยังวิกฤต เว็บเป็น JS-rendered ดึง gauge ID จุดนั้นไม่ได้ถ้าไม่มี API

## สถานะในสแต็กเราปัจจุบัน (ตรวจ 2026-09-30)

มีการคลุมเรื่องน้ำท่วมใน **ada-cms** อยู่แล้ว แต่เป็น *สรุปข่าว* ไม่ใช่ข้อมูล Flood Hub:

- **`flood-report`** (หน้า rollup "สถานการณ์น้ำท่วมล่าสุด") — รีเจนอัตโนมัติทุกชั่วโมงด้วย `flood-news-update.py`; ฟีด: `bangphli`, `samutprakan`, `bangkok-th`, `bangkok-en` (Google News RSS) มี `children: [flood-report-nongdon]`
- **`flood-report-nongdon`** — หน้า leaf ครอบคลุมฟีดสระบุรี/ลพบุรี/เขื่อนเจ้าพระยา **ยุบเมื่อ 2026-09-30**: เดิมเป็น rollup ลูกเดียวของ `flood-report-nongdon-saraburi` (ฟีดซ้ำกัน) ตัดชั้นซ้ำออก ตอนนี้ `flood-report` → `flood-report-nongdon` (leaf) โดยตรง
- ตัวสร้าง: `scripts/ada/flood-news-update.py` + `scripts/ada/flood-news-feeds.json` (repo chaba) หน้าต่างๆ ใช้ managed block `<!-- flood-news:auto -->` — จุดเสียบที่สะอาดสำหรับส่วนข้อมูลเกจอีกชุด
- Registry: collection `ada-cms-automation` ใน MDDB — หน้า generated แต่ละหน้ามี config doc (`run_now` flag → worker รีเจน; `POST /api/cms/pages/{slug}/regenerate` สั่งทันที) **จุดต้องระวัง**: registry doc cache config ของตัวเองและ**ชนะ** feeds.json — การยุบ/แยกหน้าต้องแก้ทั้ง feeds.json และ registry doc รวมถึง meta ของหน้าด้วย
- ตอนนี้ยังไม่มีอะไรใน ada-cms ใช้ข้อมูล Flood Hub/เกจ — รายงานประเมินมีแค่ใน repo doc (หน้านี้คือสำเนา)

## ประเมินบริการ

### มันคืออะไร

- ผลิตภัณฑ์ Google Research (`sites.research.google/floods` หรือ g.co/floodhub) โมเดล AI สองตัว: **hydrologic LSTM** (Nearing et al., *Nature* 627, 2024 — โมเดลที่ใช้จริง) พยากรณ์อัตราการไหล และ **inundation model** ประเมินพื้นที่+ระดับน้ำที่ได้รับผล
- พยากรณ์น้ำท่วมริมแม่น้ำ**ล่วงหน้าสูงสุด 7 วัน** อัปเดต**รายวัน** ครอบคลุม **150+ ประเทศ / ~2 พันล้านคน** ตามการตลาดปัจจุบัน (snapshot Bellingcat มิ.ย. 2025 บอก 80+ ประเทศ, จุดมั่นใจสูง 1,800+, 460 ล้านคน — ขยายมากขึ้นตั้งแต่นั้น)
- แผนที่แสดงหมุดเกจแบ่งสี (ปกติ → เฝ้าระวัง → อันตราย → วิกฤต) กราฟน้ำต่อเกจเทียบเกณฑ์, เลเยอร์พื้นที่น้ำท่วม, ประวัติน้ำท่วม, มุมมองลุ่มน้ำ การแจ้งเตือนยังโผล่ใน Google Search/Maps/Android notifications
- เกจสองแบบ: **เกจจริง** (ข้อมูลหน่วยงาน เช่น GRDC) และ **virtual HYBAS gauges** (`hybas_<id>` ช่วงแม่น้ำ HydroBASINS — ความคลุมไทยส่วนใหญ่น่าจะเป็นแบบนี้) แต่ละตัวมีแฟล็ก `qualityVerified` (โมเดลผ่านเกณฑ์ประเมินของ Google) กับ `hasModel`; UI ดีฟอลต์แสดงเฉพาะ verified, "expert mode" แสดงเกจความมั่นใจต่ำ
- ฟรีทั้งหมด ข้อมูล **CC BY 4.0** ไม่ต้องมีบัญชี มี UI ภาษาไทย (cities.google/intl/th_ALL/flood-hub)

### ข้อจำกัด (บอกตรงๆ)

- **เฉพาะน้ำในแม่น้ำ** น้ำท่วมบางพลี / ถนนเทพารักษ์ที่ `flood-report` ติดตามคือน้ำท่วมในเมือง/ระบายไม่ทัน — เกจ Flood Hub อาจไม่แสดงอะไรเลย (API มี `flashFloods:search` กับ `significantEvents:search` ที่คลุมบางส่วน — ต้องทดสอบเมื่อมี key)
- พยากรณ์เป็น**ค่าประมาณ** — เว็บเองบอก "ใช้เพื่อข้อมูลเท่านั้น ตรวจแหล่งทางการ" (ของเราคือ กรมชลฯ/thaiwater.net/ปภ.) การเทียบข้ามจำเป็นสำหรับการแจ้งเตือนที่เราเอาไปใช้
- virtual gauge ที่ไม่มี `qualityVerified` อาจผิดชัดเจน ถือเป็นเพียงคำแนะนำ
- รอบรายวัน — ไม่ใช่เซนเซอร์เรียลไทม์ โอเคสำหรับมุมมอง 1–7 วัน ใช้ไม่ได้กับเหตุระบายน้ำระดับนาที
- API ต้องรอ waitlist key ของ UI Flood Hub ฝังอยู่ฝั่ง client (โปรเจกต์ TAK-NZ ETL บันทึกว่า UI เรียก endpoint `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` สาธารณะตัวเดียวกัน) แต่ทางที่ถูกต้องคือ waitlist — ใช้ทางนั้น ไม่ใช่ key ของเขา

## การเข้าถึงแบบโปรแกรม

| รายการ | รายละเอียด |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `https://floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1` (REST, ยืนยันด้วย API key, ไม่ใช้ OAuth) |
| การเข้าถึง | ฟอร์ม waitlist → อีเมลอนุมัติ → ตอบกลับพร้อม Google Cloud Project ID → เปิดใช้ `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` |
| ค่าใช้จ่าย/ลิขสิทธิ์ | ฟรี, CC BY 4.0 |
| เมธอดหลัก | `gauges:searchGaugesByArea` (รหัสภูมิภาค `TH` หรือ polygon), `floodStatus:queryLatestFloodStatusByGaugeIds`, `floodStatus:searchLatestFloodStatusByArea`, `gauges:queryGaugeForecasts` (ค่ารายวัน 8 วัน), `gaugeModels:batchGet` (เกณฑ์เฝ้าระวัง/อันตราย/วิกฤต), `flashFloods:search`, `significantEvents:search`, `serializedPolygons/{id}` (polygon KML พื้นที่น้ำท่วม) |
| ย้อนหลัง | **Inundation History** 1999–2020 (`gs://flood-forecasting/inundation_history`), **GRRR** runoff reanalysis/reforecast 1980–2023 (ชุดข้อมูลลิงก์ Colab) |
| ทดสอบ | Google มี Colab notebook ให้ทดสอบ key |
| ข้อควรระวัง | polygon ลุ่มน้ำ HydroBASINS **ไม่มี**ใน API (TAK-NZ ยืนยัน); `serializedPolygons` คลุมเฉพาะพื้นที่น้ำท่วม |

ผู้ใช้เดิมที่น่าดูเป็นตัวอย่าง: **TAK-NZ/etl-floodhub** (poll → จุดบนแผนที่ CoT, รอบ ~120s), **Deltares DELFT-FEWS** `GoogleFloodHubV1GaugeForecast` (รูปแบบ request: `queryGaugeForecasts?gaugeIds=...&issueTimeStart=T0-25h`, batch ≤500 เกจ), **floodops** (connector Python ตาม colab ของ Google)

## แผนผสานระบบ

เรียงตามความคุ้ม/ง่าย ทุกข้อสมมติได้ waitlist ยกเว้น #1

1. **สมัคร waitlist เดี๋ยวนี้** (ไม่ต้องเขียนโค้ด) มี GCP project อยู่แล้ว (gev-gemini/Gemini API) เลือกหนึ่งตัว ส่งฟอร์มใส่ use case "home automation + local alerting" รายงานว่ารอเป็นเดือน เข้าคิวไว้ก่อน
2. **HA REST sensors บน michael-dev** (เมื่อมี key): `gauges:searchGaugesByArea` ครั้งเดียวเพื่อหาเกจไทยใกล้เรา (ลุ่มเจ้าพระยาฝั่งบางพลี + ลุ่มนครนายกสำหรับเหตุปัจจุบัน + สระบุรี/ลพบุรีสำหรับหน้า nongdon) แล้ว poll `floodStatus:queryLatestFloodStatusByGaugeIds` ทุก ~6–12 ชม. เก็บ gauge ID + เกณฑ์ไว้ใน SSOT ทำตามแพทเทิร์น `mha_mirror_*`/package ไม่ใช่ YAML ลอยๆ
3. **ต่อยอด `flood-news-update.py`** — แทนที่จะทำ job ใหม่ เพิ่ม managed block `<!-- flood-hub:auto -->` ใน `flood-report` + หน้า nongdon: ระดับเกจวันนี้ + แนวโน้ม 7 วันต่อลุ่มที่เฝ้า ข้างๆ สรุปข่าว ระบบท่อรีเจน (automation registry, `run_now`, worker) สร้างไว้แล้ว
4. **ช่องแจ้งเตือนของ Ada**: tool `flood_status` ใน ada-pi อ่าน HA entity หรือยิง API จาก idc01; severity ≥ WARNING → push ผ่าน LINE ทาง Yomi + อ่านออกเสียง ทดสอบ scenario ใน `tests/scenarios-live/` (เข้ากลุ่ม `deep_dive_flood_report`/`flood_situation` เดิม)
5. **GEV overlay**: `serializedPolygons/{id}` คืน KML พื้นที่น้ำท่วม — Cesium ใน gods-eye-view วางทับได้ งานระดับกลาง คุ้มเฉพาะช่วงมีเหตุจริงหรือเป็นเลเยอร์เสริม
6. **แบนเนอร์ display/vcast**: เกจที่เฝ้า ≥ WARNING → แบนเนอร์บนจอ vcast / CCTV wall ถูกมากถ้าทำ #2 แล้ว
7. **เทียบข้ามแหล่ง**: จับคู่ Flood Hub กับ thaiwater.net (HII) / กรมชลฯ ให้ Ada พูดได้ว่า "Google บอก X เกจกรมชลฯ บอก Y" — สอดคล้องหน้าที่ตรวจก่อนเตือน

## ช่องทางมีส่วนร่วม

- **ฟีดแบ็ก/บั๊ก**: "Send feedback" ในเว็บ + ฟอร์มบั๊กและฟอร์มฟีดแบ็กเฉพาะ ผู้เข้าร่วม pilot ขอประชุมทีมได้ — ช่องทางจริง เขาเชิญเอง
- **ข้อมูล**: คอขวดที่ Google ประกาศคือบันทึกอัตราการไหลสาธารณะ ช่องทาง: `floodforecasting@google.com` (ช่วยเผยแพร่ข้อมูล) และชุดข้อมูลเปิด **Caravan** (ช่องทางที่หน่วยงานอุทกศาสตร์ส่งข้อมูล; WMO/GRDC ป้อน 25 ประเทศผ่านมัน) **ไทยยังไม่ได้เป็นผู้ส่งข้อมูล Caravan** — ถ้ามีคนรู้จักที่กรมชลฯ/HII การผลักดันข้อมูลเกจไทยเข้า Caravan คือการมีส่วนร่วมที่คุ้มที่สุด มันจะช่วยความแม่นของ Flood Hub กับแม่น้ำที่กำลังท่วมตอนนี้โดยตรง
- **โอเพนซอร์ส**: ยังไม่มี integration Flood Hub สำหรับ Home Assistant (มีแค่ TAK/DELFT-FEWS/floodops) การเผยแพร่ config REST-sensor หรือ component HACS เล็กๆ เป็นการมีส่วนร่วมจริง — CC BY 4.0 อนุญาต
- **ground truth**: CCTV wall ของ XMEye (noble-club / noble-a) + ข้อสังเกตที่รวบรวมไว้ ใช้เทียบพยากรณ์กับความจริงในระดับท้องถิ่น; ความผิดปกติคือสิ่งที่ฟอร์มบั๊ก/การประชุม pilot ต้องการพอดี

## ขั้นตอนถัดไป

1. ~~ส่งฟอร์ม waitlist~~ — **เสร็จ 2026-09-30** ตอนนี้เฝ้าอีเมลอนุมัติ (รายงานว่าเป็นเดือน)
2. เมื่ออีเมลมาถึง: ตอบกลับด้วย Google Cloud Project ID **`flood-watch-510211`** (สร้าง 2026-09-30) → เปิดใช้ `floodforecasting.googleapis.com` → สร้าง key จำกัดเฉพาะ API + IP idc01 (`157.85.110.99`) → เก็บ `FLOODS_API_KEY` ใน `~/.config/secrets/flood-forecasting.env`
3. ทดสอบด้วย `scripts/ada/flood-hub-check.py` (พร้อมแล้ว): `gauges --region TH` แสดงเกจ, `status <id>...` แสดงระดับ/แนวโน้ม, `forecast <id>...` ดัมป์ชุด 8 วัน
4. ระหว่างนี้ `flood-report` ทำงานต่อจากข้อมูลข่าว — ไม่มีอะไรขวาง
5. ~~เก็บกวาด~~ — **เสร็จ**: ยุบ `flood-report-nongdon-saraburi` เข้า `flood-report-nongdon` (leaf); ลบหน้า CMS + เอกสาร automation ที่กำพร้า
6. เมื่อได้ key: #2 sensors → #3 managed block → #4 แจ้งเตือน Ada ส่วน GEV overlay ทำเฉพาะถ้าอยากได้มุมมองแผนที่จริง

## บันทึกอัปเดต

- **2026-09-30** — ประเมินครั้งแรก; geocode ลิงก์ได้องครักษ์ นครนายก (น้ำท่วมจากการระบายเขื่อน); ยืนยันหน้า flood-report มีและรีเจนอัตโนมัติ; ยังไม่มีข้อมูล Flood Hub ใน ada-cms
- **2026-09-30 (ช่วงหลัง)** — ส่งฟอร์ม waitlist แล้ว เพิ่ม `scripts/ada/flood-hub-check.py` + รายการ focus-inbox ติดตามการอนุมัติ
- **2026-09-30 (เย็น)** — สร้าง GCP project `flood-watch-510211` ยุบ `flood-report-nongdon-saraburi` → `flood-report-nongdon` (leaf); เรียนรู้ว่า registry cache config เองและชนะ feeds.json — การยุบต้องล้างทั้งคู่ + meta หน้า; patch `publish()` ให้ล้าง key parent/children เก่า
- **2026-09-30 (กลางคืน)** — **ทำต้นแบบ GEV flood layer** บนสาขา `flood-history-layer`: ดึง Inundation History 4 cells (สาธารณะ `gs://flood-forecasting/inundation_history`, CC-BY-4.0) คลุม lat 10.3–16.4 / lon 97.8–103.5 → รวมเป็น 3 เลเยอร์ `.geojsonl` ตามความเสี่ยง (~3.2 MB); ลงทะเบียนใน localLayers, URL tokens, enum + voice aliases เทสผ่าน, build เขียว
- **2026-09-30 (ดึก)** — **deploy แล้ว**: merge เข้า GEV main @ `f7dd661`; stage เข้า Caddy live; ยืนยัน 200 ทั้งหน้าและ asset flood ทั้ง 3; เจน `tools.json` ใหม่ + restart bridge; scenario `flood_situation` PASS เจอ regression NongDon อีกจุด + แก้: worker `ada-flood-news` จริงรันสำเนาที่ deploy บน tony-dell — sync แก้ตรงนั้น, รักษา registry+meta, audit R3 สะอาด **บทเรียน: เปลี่ยน config ของ live worker ต้อง deploy ไป `~/CascadeProjects/chaba` บน tony-dell ด้วย**

## แหล่งอ้างอิง

- developers.google.com/flood-forecasting (+ /rest reference) — พื้นผิว API, waitlist, ลิขสิทธิ์, ชุดข้อมูล, ฟอร์ม
- support.google.com/flood-hub — ข้อเท็จจริงผลิตภัณฑ์, ช่องทาง Caravan/`floodforecasting@google.com`, ความจริงของ waitlist (เดือน)
- github.com/TAK-NZ/etl-floodhub — รูปแบบการใช้ endpoint, ข้อสังเกตเรื่อง UI key, ข้อจำกัด polygon
- publicwiki.deltares.nl (DELFT-FEWS) — รูปแบบ request `queryGaugeForecasts`, เทคนิค `issueTimeStart` 25h, batch ≤500 เกจ
- github.com/bellingcat/toolkit — snapshot ความคลุม (มิ.ย. 2025), สวิตช์ verified-vs-low-confidence
- dailynews.co.th / thaipbs.or.th — บริบทเหตุนครนายกปัจจุบัน (28–29 ก.ย.)
- OSM Nominatim — geocode ตำแหน่งลิงก์ (องครักษ์, นครนายก, TH-26)
- ภายใน: `scripts/ada/flood-news-update.py` + `flood-news-feeds.json`; collection `ada-cms-pages` / `ada-cms-automation` ใน MDDB

docs.contentMd:
# รายงานข้อมูลบริการรถยกฟรี เขตบางพลี

จากการตรวจสอบข้อมูลเบื้องต้นเกี่ยวกับบริการรถยกฟรีในเขตบางพลี จังหวัดสมุทรปราการ ในช่วงสถานการณ์น้ำท่วม มีข้อมูลที่สำคัญดังนี้:

## หน่วยงานให้บริการ
*   **บก.จร. (กองบังคับการตำรวจจราจร):** มีการประชาสัมพันธ์ให้บริการรถยกฟรีเพื่อช่วยเหลือประชาชนในการเคลื่อนย้ายรถยนต์ที่ประสบปัญหาน้ำท่วมขัง โดยเน้นการเคลื่อนย้ายหลังจากระดับน้ำลดลงแล้ว สามารถติดต่อสอบถามข้อมูลเพิ่มเติมได้ที่สายด่วนตำรวจจราจร 1197

## ข้อแนะนำเพิ่มเติม
*   ประชาชนที่ต้องการความช่วยเหลือควรเตรียมข้อมูลสถานที่ที่รถจอดอยู่และจุดหมายที่ต้องการให้พ่วงลากไปให้ชัดเจน
*   ควรรวบรวมข้อมูลหน่วยงานท้องถิ่นอื่นๆ เช่น เทศบาล หรือ อบต. ในพื้นที่บางพลี ที่อาจมีมาตรการช่วยเหลือเพิ่มเติมในช่วงวิกฤต

docs.contentMd:
# รายงานข้อมูลบริการรถยกฟรี เขตพัทยา

จากการรวบรวมข้อมูลเกี่ยวกับบริการรถยกฟรีในเขตพัทยา จังหวัดชลบุรี เพื่อช่วยเหลือผู้ประสบปัญหาน้ำท่วม มีรายละเอียดดังนี้:

## หน่วยงานและช่องทางช่วยเหลือ
*   **สายด่วนเมืองพัทยา 1337:** ประชาชนสามารถติดต่อเพื่อขอความช่วยเหลือได้ตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง ซึ่งอาจรวมถึงการประสานงานเรื่องรถยกหรือการช่วยเหลือฉุกเฉินอื่นๆ
*   **บริการยกรถจากบริษัทประกันภัย:** ลูกค้าที่มีประกันภัยรถยนต์บางบริษัท (เช่น ชับบ์สามัคคีประกันภัย) ที่ประสบภัยน้ำท่วมในพื้นที่พัทยา อาจได้รับบริการยกรถฉุกเฉินฟรีตามเงื่อนไขกรมธรรม์ ควรติดต่อบริษัทประกันภัยของท่านโดยตรง

## ข้อแนะนำ
*   ตรวจสอบสิทธิ์การบริการรถยกฉุกเฉินจากกรมธรรม์ประกันภัยรถยนต์ของท่าน
*   ติดตามประกาศอย่างเป็นทางการจากเมืองพัทยาเกี่ยวกับมาตรการช่วยเหลือเพิ่มเติม

docs.contentMd:
# Gemini Deep Research agent — capability assessment for Chaba/Ada

Date: 2026-09-27 · Sources: ai.google.dev deep-research & interactions docs, Google dev blog (Dec 2025), AI Studio forum

## What it is

Google's autonomous research agent, exposed to developers via the **Interactions API**
(the new GA single endpoint for models *and* agents — `generateContent` is now legacy).
Three agents:

| Agent id | Character | Est. cost/task |
|---|---|---|
| `deep-research-preview-04-2026` | fast, streamable, ~80 queries / ~250k in / ~60k out | ~$1–3 |
| `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` | max comprehensiveness, ~160 queries / ~900k in / ~80k out | ~$3–7 |
| `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` | older Gemini 3.1 Pro version | — |

Powered by Gemini 3 Pro (SOTA on HLE + DeepSearchQA per Google; best-on-BrowseComp claim).
DeepSearchQA benchmark itself is open-sourced — usable for our own evals.

## API shape

- `interactions.create` with `agent=deep-research-*`, **`background=true` required**,
  `store=true` (retention: 55d paid / 1d free tier)
- Poll `interaction_id` until `completed`/`failed`, or `stream=true` for live steps
- `collaborative_planning=True` → agent returns a research *plan* first; a follow-up
  turn confirms/edits it before execution — **this maps 1:1 onto our confirm gates**
- `visualization="auto"` → generates charts/graphs inline in the report
- `tools` override: `google_search`, `external_data_mcp` (**it can call MCP servers**),
  `vertex_search`, File Upload/File Search for private docs (PDF/CSV)
- `service_tier="deferred"` → off-peak scheduling at **50% discount**
- Multiple concurrent background tasks allowed; label `is_deep_research` tracks cost

## Fit with our stack

### Ada voice tool — `ada_deep_research(topic, depth="standard"|"max")`

Natural fit for the dispatch/awaiting-user model:

1. Ada registers an MDDB job doc + starts interaction (`background`, `store`)
2. She answers immediately: "research queued, job X — I'll tell you when it lands"
3. A watcher (or poll-on-ask via `ada_deep_research_status`) detects completion
4. Report → `cms_publish_page` (via the new pending-confirm handshake for publish) +
   extract summary into memory bank + notify via `/api/notify`
5. Verification: CMS slug + interaction_id recorded on the job doc

The `collaborative_planning` option is the interesting one for voice: Ada reads the
plan aloud, Tony says "yes" or edits it, then she proceeds — exactly the
confirmation pattern we already want.

### Devin dispatch lanes

For project research (codebases, vendor comparisons): the dispatch JSONL ledger
already models long-running jobs — DR calls could be steps inside dispatched
sessions rather than separate plumbing.

### NotebookLM

DR is coming to NotebookLM natively — overlaps our NotebookLM summarization path;
watch for it replacing our digest step rather than duplicating it.

### Benchmarking

DeepSearchQA (open-source, Google) = a real benchmark corpus for complex web
research — could score Ada's `web_search`+synthesis path against DR directly.

## Constraints / watch-outs

- **Preview** — agents ids are dated previews; expect churn
- **Paid tier required** — our key is free tier now (web_search hit the 20/day
  grounding cap today); DR has no free quota worth using; also API keys must be
  restricted to generativelanguage.googleapis.com by June 2026 policy
- Runs take **minutes** — never inline on a live voice turn; always background
- Retention: free=1d (too short for our job ledger), paid=55d — we must snapshot
  the report to MDDB/CMS on completion regardless
- `store=true` means queries live on Google's side — no sensitive content in prompts

## Recommendation

Yes — adopt as Ada's `ada_deep_research` tool (standard tier default, `max` opt-in,
`deferred` when not urgent). It's the strongest missing piece between quick
`web_search` and full Devin dispatch: ~$1–3 for a cited multi-source report lands
squarely in our "control desk → job → notify → verify" architecture.

Prereqs: paid-tier API key (restricted scope), watcher for completion,
CMS publish on land. MVP ~half a day of plumbing.

# Gemini & OR Embedding Benchmark

Run 2026-10-02T23:01:01Z — 29 real `ada-cms-pages` docs, 768 dims.
Direct = `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` batchEmbedContents;
OR = `google/gemini-embedding-2` via OpenRouter (provider order: Google Vertex).

## Verdict

**Same vector space — OR is a drop-in mirror, safe to keep.**

| metric | direct Gemini | OpenRouter |
|---|---|---|
| latency p50 (10-doc batch) | 1.72s | 6.54s |
| latency worst batch | 1.77s | 7.02s |
| top-1 retrieval probes | 8/8 | 8/8 |

cosine(OR, direct) per doc — mean **1.0**, min **1.0**
(≈1.0 = identical space; same underlying model via Vertex).

## Cost

- OR billed tokens this run: **12221** ≈ **$0.00183**
  (at $0.15/Mtok — recheck OR pricing if it shifts).
- Projected: mddb daily writes ≈ tens of docs → **< $0.01/month** steady state;
  full-corpus re-embed ≈ a few cents one-shot.
- Comparison for *search* (not embeddings): Gemini paid grounding is
  ~$35/1K queries vs OR online/sonar routes ~$4-5/1K — the bigger
  argument for OR lives there; free-tier grounding stays at 20/day.

## Routes measured

- Primary (live): `gemini-ollama-proxy` → OR `google/gemini-embedding-2`
- Backup chain in proxy: OR → direct Gemini → local Ollama (`nomic-embed-text`)
- Hard-fail on OR error is deliberate — a different-space fallback would
  poison retrieval silently.

## Pros & cons of keeping OR in parallel

**Pros**
- Same vector space proven (cosine 1.000) — OR is a true mirror, no
  re-embed or collection migration ever needed.
- Off the Gemini free tier — embeddings no longer share the 20-req/day
  budget with grounded `web_search` and voice traffic.
- Predictable spend: measured **$0.0016/run**; steady state < $0.01/mo.
- Chain stays intact on OR outage: OR → (direct Gemini) → local Ollama.

**Cons**
- ~5× slower per batch — OR's Vertex route rejects array input, so every
  text is its own HTTP call (fine at our write volume). OR docs claim
  arrays are supported; the pin to provider `Google` is what breaks it.
- Silent spend creep — needs an occasional usage check, not alerts.
- OR AI-Studio provider route is broken (bogus API_KEY_INVALID) —
  pinned `order:[Google]` is the only working path.

## Improvements — applied vs open

**Applied this run**
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` restored in `mddb-gemini.env` + proxy now falls back
  to direct Gemini (same space, verified 1.000) on OR failure — Ollama
  still refused. Failover tested live: dead OR → direct Gemini → 768d.
- **int8 quantization set on all 40 collections** (`/v1/collection-config`).
  Applies to new writes + the in-memory index; existing float32 storage
  stays readable.

**Live observations during rollout**
- The cold-start vector-index rebuild took **>75 min at ~96% CPU** on
  ~11.6K vectors / 3.4GB DB — vector-search 503s the entire time
  (500+ failed calls; Ada semantic recall degraded during rebuilds).
  Cold-index rebuild is mddb's main operational weakness on this host.
- mddb flagged **18 collections with stale embedding provenance**
  (pre-gemini-embedding-2 space) and auto-re-embeds them through the
  proxy at ~2 calls/min — OR-sequential latency again.
- `POST /v1/vector-reindex` exists and is cheap to call.

**Open (ranked)**
1. **Scheduled `vector-reindex` for the 18 mismatched collections**
   (provenance cleanup — do during off-hours; costs pennies in OR).
2. **OR search tier for `web_search`** — paid Gemini grounding ≈ $35/1K
   vs OR sonar ≈ $5/1K; sits between free-20/day and DuckDuckGo.
3. **Chunk-size tuning** — mddb chunks at 1500 chars; each chunk is one
   sequential OR call → the 20s+ CMS write times. Larger chunks or
   proxy concurrency would cut it.
4. **Parallelize OR embed calls** (4-8 concurrent) in the proxy.
5. **Weekly `embed-bench` timer + OR usage readout.**
6. **Pin `dimensions:768` + model in SSOT.**
7. **OR Batch API** exists for embeddings (async, `provider.only` pin)
   — right tool for bulk re-embeds, not live writes.

## Sources

- mddb quantization: github.com/tradik/mddb → docs/QUANTIZATION.md
- mddb chunking/cache: docs/features + EMBEDDING_PROVIDERS.md
- OR embeddings spec: openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/embeddings
- OR batch API: openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart

# Gesture UI — ada_v2 complete implementation reference + YOLO assessment

Self-contained reference for rebuilding the ada_v2 hand-gesture UI. Everything
needed is in this file — no re-digging the archive required.

**Source of truth:** `tonezzz/ada` (archived) @ `af6d57223f72fce68b4d6f47bbfc6a75b7bc0085`
— `ada_v2/src/App.jsx` (gesture pipeline lines ~1068–1558, window manager
~339–413, ~510–536, ~1720–1876, render ~1919–2238), `ada_v2/package.json`,
`ada_v2/electron/main.js`, `ada_v2/src/index.css`,
`ada_v2/src/components/ToolsModule.jsx`, `ada_v2/backend/server.py`,
`ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py`, `ada_v2/README.md`.

## Architecture at a glance

```
Webcam (getUserMedia 1920x1080)
  -> <video> (hidden, opacity-0)
  -> requestAnimationFrame(predictWebcam)        ~60fps when video on
       |- drawImage -> visible <canvas>          (CAM_01 tile, optional mirror)
       |- every 5th frame -> 640x360 canvas -> JPEG q0.6
       |     -> socket.emit('video_frame')       -> backend ada.py
       |     -> audio_loop.send_frame -> Gemini Live vision  (side-channel)
       '- if handTracking enabled && new video frame:
             detectForVideo -> 21 normalized landmarks
             -> fingertip cursor math -> pinch click / fist drag
             -> cyan skeleton drawn on canvas
```

All gesture interpretation is **browser-local**. The backend never saw gesture
events — the two paths (UI control vs AI vision) are fully independent.

## Dependencies & assets

- `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` `^0.10.22-rc.20250304` (npm dep in package.json)
- WASM runtime loaded from CDN: `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm")` —
  **note the version skew** (CDN pinned @0.10.0 vs npm rc-20250304)
- Model: `/hand_landmarker.task` served from `public/` (~7.8 MB, Google's stock
  HandLandmarker full model)
- React 18, socket.io-client 4.7.4, electron 28, vite 5, lucide-react icons
- Electron: frameless 1920x1080 window (`frame: false`); top bar uses
  `WebkitAppRegion: 'drag'` (mouse-only OS window drag)

## Init sequence (runs once, guarded)

```js
const vision = await FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm");
handLandmarkerRef.current = await HandLandmarker.createFromOptions(vision, {
    baseOptions: { modelAssetPath: "/hand_landmarker.task", delegate: "GPU" },
    runningMode: "VIDEO",
    numHands: 1
});
```

- First `fetch('/hand_landmarker.task')` verifies the file exists (logs
  content-type/length) before creating the landmarker.
- Guarded by `handLandmarkerInitStartedRef` — init runs once on mount.
- Success posts "Hand Tracking Ready" to the chat; failure posts the error.

## Capture & loop

- `getUserMedia({ video: { width: ideal 1920, height: ideal 1080,
  aspectRatio: 16/9, deviceId? } })` -> `video.srcObject` -> `play()`.
- `predictWebcam` runs via `requestAnimationFrame` only while `isVideoOn`.
- Guards: bail if `video.readyState < 2` or `videoWidth/Height === 0`
  (prevents MediaPipe crash on cold start).
- Dedup: `video.currentTime !== lastVideoTimeRef` — skips inference on
  repeated frames.
- `detectForVideo(video, performance.now())` — needs monotonic ms timestamp.
- Hand tracking requires **video ON** (`isVideoOn`) **and** the Hand toggle
  (`isHandTrackingEnabled`, default OFF) — two separate switches.
- FPS counter displayed in top bar while video is on.

## Constants (verified from source)

| Constant | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|
| SENSITIVITY | `cursorSensitivity`, default **2.0** | settings slider; center 50% of camera maps to 100% of screen |
| LERP | **0.2** | `smoothedCursorPos += (target - smoothed) * 0.2` |
| SNAP_THRESHOLD | **50 px** | snap cursor to closest interactive element's center |
| UNSNAP_THRESHOLD | **100 px** | hysteresis — must pass 100px to release |
| PINCH threshold | **0.05** | normalized `dist(lm4, lm8)` |
| Drag deadzone | **0.5 px** | ignore wrist deltas below this |
| Transmission | **640x360, JPEG q0.6, every 5th frame** | `video_frame` socket event |
| numHands | **1** | second hand ignored |
| z base | **30** | `getZIndex = 30 + index in zIndexOrder` |

## Cursor math (per detected frame)

```js
rawX   = isCameraFlipped ? 1 - lm8.x : lm8.x;   // optional mirror
normX  = clamp((rawX - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);
normY  = clamp((lm8.y - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);   // y not flipped
target = normX * innerWidth, normY * innerHeight;
smoothed += (target - smoothed) * 0.2;          // lerp
finalX/finalY = smoothed (unless snapped);
```

**Snap hysteresis** — every frame scans
`document.querySelectorAll('button, input, select, .draggable')`, finds the
element whose **rect center** is nearest the cursor; if `dist < 50px` the
cursor locks to that center and the element gets a cyan glow
(`boxShadow 0 0 20px rgba(34,211,238,.6)`, `backgroundColor rgba(6,182,212,.2)`,
`borderColor cyan` — all **inline styles**; `.snap-highlight` class is added
but has no CSS). Releases only when cursor drifts `> 100px` from the snap
point.

## Pinch = click

- `dist(lm4, lm8) < 0.05` in normalized coordinates.
- **Rising edge only**: fires when `isPinchNow && !isPinching` — one click per
  pinch, hold doesn't repeat.
- Hit-test: `document.elementFromPoint(finalX, finalY)` then
  `el.closest('button, input, a, [role="button"]')` -> `.click()`; falls back
  to `el.click()` if no clickable ancestor.
- Consequence: pinch fires `.click()` but **not** mousedown/mouseup — elements
  driven by pointer-down handlers (drag handles, 3D canvas) don't respond to
  pinch. Dragging is fist-only.

## Fist = grab/drag window

```js
isFingerFolded(tip, mcp) = dist(tip, lm0_wrist) < dist(mcp, lm0_wrist)
isFist = folded(8,5) && folded(12,9) && folded(16,13) && folded(20,17)
         // index, middle, ring, pinky — thumb NOT checked
```

- On fist, if no drag active: hit-test cursor against `getBoundingClientRect()`
  of **`['cad','browser','kasa','printer']`** (popup window ids only) — cursor
  inside rect -> `activeDragElement = id`, `bringToFront(id)`, lock wrist pos.
- While fist held: compute **wrist (lm0)** screen pos with the same
  flip/sensitivity/clamp math (no lerp), delta vs last wrist pos; apply via
  `updateElementPosition(id, dx, dy)` when `|dx|>0.5 || |dy|>0.5`.
- Wrist (not fingertip) is used because the wrist doesn't move while forming
  the fist — fingertip would jump.
- Any non-fist frame releases (`activeDragElement = null`). The README's
  "open palm = release" is just the natural non-fist pose.
- `activeDragElement` also drives a green ring highlight on the grabbed window.

## Window manager contract (what gestures manipulate)

- `elementPositions` / `elementSizes` maps; **anchors differ per element**:
  - `chat`: top-center (`translate(-50%,0)`) — x=中心, y=top edge
  - `video`: top-left
  - everything else: center (`translate(-50%,-50%)`)
- `updateElementPosition` clamps to viewport bounds per anchor type
  (margin 0); `clampToViewport` (margin 10, topBar 60) is used for popup
  initial placement.
- `zIndexOrder` array; `getZIndex = 30 + index`; `bringToFront` moves id to
  end of array.
- `fixedElements = ['visualizer','chat','video','tools']` — never mouse-draggable.
- Mouse path: `handleMouseDown` requires `[data-drag-handle]` inside the
  target **unless** modular mode is on; blocks drag start on
  input/button/textarea/canvas. Fist-drag bypasses the handle requirement and
  works anywhere inside the four popup rects.
- Popup visibility toggles (`showCadWindow` etc.) come from socket events
  (`cad_data`, `browser_frame`, `request_print_window`) or ToolsModule buttons.

## DOM contract for a rebuild

- Hidden `<video>` (opacity-0) + visible `<canvas>` (80% opacity, optional
  `scaleX(-1)` mirror) inside a `w-80 aspect-video` tile labeled CAM_01,
  fixed bottom-right, id=`video`, z=20.
- Cursor: `fixed w-6 h-6 border-2 rounded-full pointer-events-none z-[100]`
  cyan ring + white center dot at `{left: cursorPos.x, top: cursorPos.y,
  transform: translate(-50%,-50%)}`; while pinching it gets
  `bg-cyan-400 scale-75` + stronger glow.
- Popup windows: `id={cad|browser|kasa|printer}`, positioned `absolute` at
  `elementPositions[id]` with `translate(-50%,-50%)`, `zIndex: getZIndex(id)`,
  `data-drag-handle` on their header bars for mouse drag.
- Hand toggle: `Hand` icon button in bottom `ToolsModule` toolbar — orange
  border/glow when enabled.
- Settings: `SettingsWindow` exposes `cursorSensitivity` slider +
  `isCameraFlipped` checkbox; **flip is persisted server-side** —
  backend `settings.json` key `camera_flipped`, pushed on `settings` socket
  event, applied via `setIsCameraFlipped`. (Sensitivity stays client-side.)

## Debug/visual aids

- `drawSkeleton`: cyan `HAND_CONNECTIONS` lines on the display canvas at
  native resolution.
- Logging: "Tracking loop running... Hand Found/No Hand" every 100 frames;
  "First hand detection!" once.
- Removed features still referenced: `cursorTrailRef`, `ripples` state,
  "Trail Logic"/"Ripple Effect" comments — dead code, don't port.

## Worked trace with real values

Cursor — index tip `lm8=(0.58, 0.30)`, screen 1920x1080, SENSITIVITY=2.0:

```
norm    = ((0.58-.5)*2+.5, (0.30-.5)*2+.5)  =  (0.66, 0.10)
target  = (1267, 108) px
lerp a=0.2:  f1 (253,22) -> f3 (618,53) -> f6 (935,80) -> ... -> (1267,108)
```

Snap — button center at (1264,198): dist 16px < 50 -> snaps & locks; drift
60px -> still glued (<=100); drift 120px -> unsnaps.

Pinch — `dist(lm4,lm8) = 0.0071 < 0.05` -> rising edge -> elementFromPoint ->
`.closest('button…').click()`.

Fist drag — all four tips closer to wrist than their MCPs -> cursor inside
`cad` rect -> grab; wrist `(0.55,0.62)->(0.58,0.60)` -> screen
`(1152,799)->(1267,756)` -> `updateElementPosition('cad', +115, -43)`.

## Edge cases & sharp edges

- `numHands: 1` — a second hand is silently ignored; `landmarks[0]` wins.
- Smoothed cursor starts at (0,0) — first frames lerp in from the corner;
  `lastWristPos` only locks on grab so drag doesn't jump.
- Snap scan is O(all interactive DOM nodes) every frame — fine at this scale,
  cache the list if porting to a bigger DOM.
- Fist hit-test uses the *smoothed/snapped* cursor position (finalX/finalY),
  not the wrist — so you aim with the fingertip, then clench.
- Thumb isn't part of the fist check — thumb-out fist still counts (and is
  required for the pinch detector to not conflict).
- `elementFromPoint` ignores `pointer-events-none` layers (cursor, noise,
  backdrop) — by design they can't be clicked or hit-tested.
- No scroll gesture, no right-click, no two-hand gestures, no dwell click.
- Browser/Safari: MediaPipe WASM works but needs a secure context and a user
  gesture for camera permission; iOS standalone-PWA mic issues are
  audio-specific but camera in PWA mode is its own gamble — test early.
- CDN WASM pin (@0.10.0) vs npm dep (0.10.22-rc) mismatch — vendor both for
  a rebuild (same pattern as vendored echarts `/local/` assets on HA hosts).

## Can YOLO do it?

Not directly — wrong-shaped output. YOLO detection gives bounding boxes +
class labels; the ada_v2 UX needs continuous 21-point landmark geometry
(fingertip pointer, sub-pixel pinch distance).

| Requirement | YOLO detection | YOLO-pose (keypoints) |
|---|---|---|
| Fingertip cursor (sub-pixel) | box centre only — too coarse | yes, if trained on hand-keypoint data |
| Pinch distance | not possible | yes |
| Fist/palm classification | yes (train classes, e.g. HaGRID) | derived from keypoints |

### Pros

- **Range/scale** — MediaPipe's palm detector drops hands beyond ~1-2 m; a
  YOLO trained on diverse data detects raised hands across a room (kiosk /
  wall tablet / TV surfaces).
- **Multi-hand/multi-person** tracking is more robust at distance.
- **Vocabulary growth** — new poses = retrain, no hand-tuned landmark
  heuristics (ada_v2's folded-finger check is brittle: ignores thumb, 2-D only).
- Easy server-side GPU inference via ultralytics.

### Cons

- Boxes != landmarks — gesture-class YOLO loses the pointer UX that made it
  feel like Minority Report.
- Custom data/training burden beyond HaGRID's vocabulary.
- Latency — browser WASM/WebGPU MediaPipe runs ~60 fps locally; a server
  round-trip adds 30-100 ms, felt immediately in a pointer UI.
- In-browser YOLO (TFJS/ONNX.js) is heavier than MediaPipe WASM.
- On Pi-class hardware (ada-pi): YOLO won't hit interactive rates on CPU;
  MediaPipe TFLite gets ~15-30 fps on Pi 5, or needs the Hailo AI HAT.

## Recommendation

1. **Keep MediaPipe** if reviving for ada-pi/PWA — or bump to `tasks-vision`
   WebGPU delegate, or `GestureRecognizer` (prebuilt classes: closed fist,
   open palm, point-up, thumbs up/down, victory). The feature was dropped for
   product reasons, not because it failed.
2. **Use YOLO where it wins** — a "hand raised" wake/attention gesture for
   room-scale surfaces. Hybrid: cheap YOLO watch -> activate the landmark
   pipeline only while a hand is up.
3. **Keep the UX layer** — lerp smoothing, snap-with-hysteresis, wrist-delta
   dragging are model-agnostic and made it usable. With YOLO classes add
   N-of-M temporal voting to stop label flicker.
4. **Pi hardware** — prefer inference in the PWA (browser already has webcam +
   GPU) over streaming frames to a GPU server; privacy and latency both better.

Net: YOLO can do gesture *recognition*; ada_v2 was a landmark-driven
*pointer system*. For that, MediaPipe (or any 21-keypoint model) is the
right primitive. YOLO is the answer only if the goal shifts to room-scale,
discrete, multi-person gestures.

## Rebuild checklist (ada-pi / PWA)

1. Vendor `hand_landmarker.task` + tasks-vision WASM locally (no CDN
   dependency; version-lock both to the same release).
2. Port `predictWebcam` verbatim: readyState guard -> canvas draw ->
   (optional) backend frame relay -> landmark pipeline.
3. Port cursor pipeline: flip -> sensitivity -> clamp -> lerp -> snap
   hysteresis -> setCursorPos; DOM cursor div; pinch/fist state machines;
   wrist-delta drag + bounds-by-anchor.
4. Recreate the DOM contract: popup ids, `data-drag-handle`, snap target
   selector, cursor div, Hand toggle button, settings (sensitivity + flip).
5. Decide persistence: ada_v2 kept `camera_flipped` in backend settings.json —
   in ada-pi pick the equivalent (HA input_boolean / PWA localStorage /
   backend settings file).
6. Improve on it: add dwell-click or N-of-M pinch voting, second-hand support
   (`numHands: 2`), `GestureRecognizer` for extra vocabulary, wake-word-style
   "hand up" gate to save GPU when idle.

## References

- Archive report: `docs/kb/archive/ada/ada-v2-platform.md`
- Manifest: `docs/archive/manifests/ada.yml`
- Source: `tonezzz/ada` @ `af6d572` — `ada_v2/src/App.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/src/components/{ToolsModule,SettingsWindow,...}.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/backend/server.py`, `ada_v2/electron/main.js`,
  `ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py` (standalone OpenCV prototype — wider vocab
  incl. directional pointing + peace sign; scratch code, not shipped),
  `ada_v2/README.md`, `ada_v2/package.json`

- 2026-10-07T18:21 Reviewed gesture report; added YOLO feasibility details and Pi reference.
- 2026-10-07T18:22 Reviewed gesture report; added YOLO feasibility details and Pi reference.

# GEV Screen Interaction Benchmark

`gev_screen1_interact` — Ada casts God's Eye View to vcast screen 1 and drives it incrementally. 6 turns: cast → what's showing → fly to Bangkok → zoom to globe → verify view state → stop cast.

## Result

| Run | Expectations | Functional outcome |
|-----|--------------|--------------------|
| run 1 | PASS (0 failed) | cast OK; every `gev_command` hit relay 404 — relay was never deployed |
| run 2 | PASS | `gev_command` called but errored `urllib not defined` — latent bug |
| run 3 | **PASS, functional** | cast → fly Bangkok → zoom globe → state query all delivered to live GEV client |

## Chain verified end-to-end

`Ada tool gev_command` → `POST /apps/gev-cmd/command` → gev-gemini bridge → `function_call` frame → browser clients → `runTool(runner)` executes on the casted page.

## Bugs found & fixed this run

1. **Caddy route missing** — repo `stacks/web/Caddyfile` had `/apps/gev-cmd/*` since commit `472f5a0a` but it was never deployed; running edge had no route (404). Also discovered `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` had reverted to the stock 13-line template — the entire apps edge was one reload away from total loss; the real config (with gev-cmd) is now on disk and validated on caddy 2.6.2.
2. **Bridge image stale** — deployed `gev-gemini` predated the `/command` endpoint; image rebuilt + restarted.
3. **`gev_command` crash** — `urllib.request` used without import (the import lived inside a sibling method). ada-pi `54ab1c2`.
4. **Passive displays unreachable** — the bridge only counted voice-session sockets as clients; a casted page never registered. **New:** `?remote=1` ws = command-only client, no Gemini Live session (zero quota cost). GEV `index.html` now opens the remote socket at page parse (before Cesium init) and queues commands until the action runner is ready; `gevGeminiRealtime.js` registers a listener after `initGevVoiceCommands`. Live-verified: `/command/health` reports `{clients, remote}`, commands deliver to casted screens.

## Caveats

- **Fire-and-forget**: `/command` returns `delivered` count only — `get_current_view_state` reaches the client but its result doesn't come back through the relay. Verification loop is Ada → relay → screen state, not client-returned state.
- **Broadcast**: commands go to every connected GEV page — if two screens show GEV they both fly.
- **Display must be awake**: iPad suspended = page JS dead = no remote client (screen 1 stayed remote:0 while asleep; screen 2's desktop browser connected instantly).
- Commands on a still-initializing page queue until the action runner exists (early ws + 2s drain).

## Files

- scenario: `ada-pi/tests/scenarios-live/gev_screen1_interact.yaml` (tier: full)
- bridge: `chaba/stacks/tony-dell/gev-gemini/bridge.py` (`REMOTE` set + `?remote=1` path)
- frontend: `gods-eye-view` `index.html` early listener + `src/voice/gevGeminiRealtime.js` `initGevRemoteListener`
- edge: `chaba/stacks/web/Caddyfile` `/apps/gev-cmd/*` → `127.0.0.1:8790` (deployed via admin API + persisted to /etc/caddy)

## Next

- Tool-response return path: bridge waits briefly for remote client's `tool_response` so `get_current_view_state` can answer Ada.
- Screen-scoped commands: `screen=N` arg so broadcast doesn't hit every GEV page.
- iPad wake hook: vcast wakeLock exists but iOS still suspends background tabs.

## Screen narration (added same session)

`vcast_say(screen, text)` — Ada speaks short narration through the display's
own speechSynthesis ("Flying the map to Bangkok"). Implemented:
- vcast `speak` message handler (`stacks/web/public/apps/vcast/index.html`)
- tool `vcast_say` in ada-pi (owner-gated like cast_to_screen; in ACTUATING_TOOLS)
- tool description nudges Ada to announce screen actions inline.
iOS gates speech behind one user tap on the display's "audio" button; before
that the display shows the line as a toast and reports `speak-blocked`.
A sleeping iPad runs no page JS — narration requires the screen awake.

## Verification loop + screen targeting (added 2026-09-29)

The relay is no longer fire-and-forget:
- `POST /command` accepts `{name, args, screen?, wait?}` — `screen:N`
  targets only remotes whose hello announced that vcast screen (the
  same-origin iframe reads `parent.__vcastScreen`; also `?screen=N` url
  param); `wait:>0` collects `tool_response` frames and returns them in
  `responses` — `get_current_view_state` can now actually answer Ada.
- Remote clients announce `{type:'hello', screen}` on ws open (+6s/+20s
  retries — the vcast 'registered' msg races the socket open).
- `/command/health` reports `remote_screens` for debugging.
- Verified end-to-end: hello'd screen-3 python client received a
  screen-scoped command and its tool_response came back in the POST body.
- `gev_command` tool args: `screen` + `wait` (default 3s).

Operational note: displays must be RELOADED to pick up new vcast/GEV
page code — connected screens run whatever JS was loaded at boot
(`{"type":"reload"}` via /pub). Pages still initializing queue commands
until the action runner exists.

## Update — bundle corruption root-caused (2026-09-29)

The 'still initializing' mystery on real browsers was a **corrupted
bundle**: an early path-prefix sed ran unanchored on `dist/` and broke JS
syntax (`Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '/'` — no page JS ran at
all). Fixed: clean `npm run build` + quote-anchored `/api/`/`/models/`
prefixes only; `node --check` gates deploy now. Lesson: never regex-patch
minified bundles without a syntax check.

Also verified live:
- `uplink_confirm_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm-gate before camera
  uplink, acknowledge running capture, clean stop, lease cleared)
- `cast_switch_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm gates, source switch,
  busy-destination check, move, teardown). Notably strict consent:
  'screen 4 is free' was NOT accepted as camera permission — she asked
  again explicitly.

## gev_screen4_interact — FULL PASS (2026-09-29)

All 7 turns green on a live browser display: cast → confirm → describe →
fly Bangkok → zoom globe → verify (real view-state returned in
`responses` — Ada honestly reported ~18,000km near Austin, i.e. drifted
from Bangkok after zoom-out) → stop.

Two bugs this run flushed out:

1. **Cross-session speaker bleed** — a concurrent `simulate_speaker=KK`
   scenario flipped the shared runner's `current_speaker_ha_person` and
   MY session's cast/gev calls were denied as `person.kk` (owner-gated).
   Fixed: `execute()` takes `speaker=` via `_CALLER_SPEAKER` contextvar;
   explicit None (unidentified session) no longer falls back to the
   shared field. ada-pi `012dee9` + `e73a15f`, 58 unit tests green.
2. **Phantom assertion keys** — `result_contains_any` and quoted
   substrings (`"ok": true`) silently no-op'd/missed because tool results
   arrive JSON-escaped in events. Assertions rewritten escape-agnostic
   (`delivered`, `responses` bare; both `": 0` serializations blocked).

# God's Eye View — development jobs & Ada control plan

Platform: Cesium geospatial app (`gods-eye-view`), Gemini Live voice
bridge `gev-gemini` (:8789) + **command relay `/command` (:8790,
Caddy `/apps/gev-cmd/*`)** — drives connected GEV clients without voice.

## Verified live (2026-09-30)

- `POST /apps/gev-cmd/command {name,args,screen,pane,wait}` →
  `function_call` frame → client executes + returns `tool_response`
- Tested: `fly_to_location {query:"Bangkok"}` → camera at
  `lat 13.75 lon 100.49` in a headless GEV client
- Ada tool `gev_command(name,args,screen,pane,wait)` deployed on idc01
  (ada-ha-tony restarted 11:58) with full schema guidance
- Remote clients register `?remote=1` + `hello {screen,pane}` — casted
  GEV pages are individually targetable

## The flow that works today

1. `Ada, cast God's Eye View to screen N` → `cast_to_screen nav /apps/gev/`
2. `Ada, fly to Bangkok` → `gev_command fly_to_location {query}` → TV flies
3. `Ada, what's showing?` → `gev_command get_current_view_state` → answers

## Development jobs

| # | job | status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `POST /command` bridge relay | **done + deployed** (screen/pane targeting, response wait, coord normalization) |
| 2 | Ada `gev_command` tool + schema coaching | **done + deployed** |
| 3 | `gev_cast_control` scenario | written, queued behind scenario lock |
| 4 | vcast smoothness audit | relay 183ms pub; GEV renders in iframe; pending-claim UX gap open |
| 5 | CMS mobile UX | done (collapse/filter/highlight) |
| 6 | turn-stall watchdog | deployed 09-27 (`5c9095d`) — watch `live_stalled` |

## Open issues

- 2 stale `remote_pending` clients (unannounced screens) — likely test
  pages; idle cleanup in bridge would tidy them
- `vcast-screen-cast` scenario failing 2 runs (09-29) — investigate
- New-device claim flow still manual (`/claim`) — Ada can't self-assign
- Phantom write claim flagged 09-29 08:12 ("GEV is now on scr…" with no
  tool call) — the scenario's `no_failed_result` guard targets this

the 06:46 fleet audit delta readings (omen load 98.69 pre-fix).

## Host status

| Host | Uptime | Load (1/5/15) | RAM used | Swap | Disk | Verdict |

subject: hosting-provider-assessment
title: Hosting Provider Assessment

docs.contentMd:
# Hosting Provider Assessment

_2026-09-27 · Devin · idc02 spec: Linux · ≥4 vCPU · ≥16GB RAM · ≥200GB SSD · daily backups · ~฿800/mo_


**See also:** [International Hosting Providers — latency-checked shortlist](https://idc03.taila0626a.ts.net/cms/#/hosting-provider-intl) (2026-10-07 — offshore candidates with measured + published latency for Manila, Oslo, Frankfurt, Bangkok, Chonburi, Khao Yai).

## Shortlist

| Provider / Plan | vCPU | RAM | SSD | Price/mo | DC | Meets spec? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS** | 4 | 16 GB | 300 GB | ฿800 (+7% VAT = ฿856) | Thailand | ✅ exact fit, at budget |
| **ReadyIDC VPS Game LG2SS+** | 8 | 18 GB | 150 GB | ฿800 | Thailand | ⚠️ storage short 50GB |
| ReadyIDC VPS Game LG3SS+ | 10 | 26 GB | 200 GB | ฿1,100 | Thailand | ✅ over budget 37% |
| **Contabo Cloud VPS 8** | 8 | 24 GB | 300 GB | €11.20 (~฿420, 24-mo price; €14 list) | **Singapore** | ✅ 2× spec at half price |
| Hetzner CPX41 | 8 | 16 GB | 240 GB NVMe | €23.29 (~฿880) + backups ~20% → ~฿1,050 | EU (SIN ~$39 = ฿1,370) | ✅ over budget ~30% |
| _reference: Siamdata (idc01)_ | — | — | — | ฿800-ish | Thailand | existing provider |

## Caveats that decide this

**Backups are not free anywhere.** None of the plans include daily
backups by default — Hetzner auto-backup is +20%, Contabo gives 3
snapshots (manual), ReadyIDC sells backup as a separate product line.
The spec's "daily backups included" effectively means *self-managed
backup* (our mddb-backup.timer pattern) regardless of provider — do
not pay extra for it unless it's a real managed service.

**Contabo's price is real but so is its reputation**: oversubscribed
hosts, CPU steal at peak hours, ticket support measured in days. For
mddb's sustained-index-rebuild workload — exactly what saturated idc01 —
Contabo is a coin flip. Fine for Chaba Lab; risky for production mddb.

**Latency**: Thai DC ~1–5ms from home; Singapore ~10–30ms; EU ~180ms.
For an Ada-facing node, SIN is acceptable, EU is not for interactive
paths (but fine for batch memory/index workloads).

**Provider-correlation risk still stands**: a second Siamdata box shares
the failure modes of idc01. ReadyIDC is a different Thai operator —
same latency, different blast radius. That argues *for* ReadyIDC over
a second Siamdata.

## Recommendation

1. **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS (฿856 incl. VAT)** — meets the spec
   *exactly* at budget, Thai DC (voice-adjacent latency), independent
   provider (no correlation with Siamdata), Thai support. The
   straightforward idc02 pick.
2. **Contabo Cloud VPS 8 (~฿420)** — if the node is for Lab/bench
   workloads where occasional CPU-steal hurts nothing. Twice the spec
   at half the price; just don't put production mddb there without a
   soak test.
3. **Hetzner CPX41 (~฿1,050 w/ backups)** — if quality/API maturity
   beats budget. Over budget but the cleanest ops story (Terraform,
   hourly billing, snapshot API). EU latency fine for batch, not for
   Ada-facing services.

**Public IP optional**: with the Cloudflare Tunnel edge (see
`chaba-edge-plan`), idc02 does not need its own public IPv4 — outbound
cloudflared covers "public" reach, and tailnet covers admin. That
removes the included-IP line from the decision and slightly favors
the cheapest spec-fit (Contabo) — though ReadyIDC remains the pick for
provider independence + Thai latency.

**Keep the original split either way**: mddb/indexing on idc02, Ada +
edge stays on idc01, tailnet-only, replicate-then-cutover.

| Vultr — `fra-de-ping.vultr.com` | Frankfurt, DE | **194.7 ms** | measured |
| OVH — `proof.ovh.net` | France | **216.5 ms** | measured |
| OVH — `ping.ovh.net` | France | **255.3 ms** | measured |
| Hetzner — `fsn1-speed.hetzner.com` | Falkenstein, DE | **275.8 ms** | measured (jittery, mdev 14 ms — likely suboptimal routing on this ISP) |

No-ICMP endpoints (filtered, not dead): DigitalOcean `speedtest-*`,
Hetzner `speed.hetzner.de` / `nb1-speed`, Vultr `nrt`/`lax`, GCP
`gcping.com` (HTTP-only ping tool), Oracle speedtest.

## Latency by target location (published / estimated)

All figures in this section are **published or estimated** — only the
Thailand column above is measured by us.

**Philippines (Manila)** — Philippine traffic for SEA is best served from
Hong Kong or Singapore; both are one submarine hop away.

| Destination | RTT | Source |
|---|---|---|
| → Hong Kong DC | ~17–45 ms | published: Dataplugs looking glass 21 ms, Zenlayer Manila 32 ms, Tencent SEA matrix 45 ms |
| → Singapore DC | ~25–51 ms | published: Tencent 25 ms, Zenlayer 38 ms, WonderNetwork ~51 ms |
| → Frankfurt | ~141 ms | estimated (OnionVPS Manila table — great-circle floor) |

**Norway (Oslo)** — Nordics peer into EU core; Asia is a far hop.

| Destination | RTT | Source |
|---|---|---|
| → Frankfurt / German DCs | ~25–35 ms | published-typical (Oslo–FRA fibre norms) |
| → Helsinki (Hetzner FI) | ~15–25 ms | published-typical |
| → Singapore | ~170–190 ms | estimated |
| → Hong Kong / Thailand | ~200–240 ms | estimated |

**Germany** — local DCs are effectively free latency-wise; Asia is long-haul.

| Destination | RTT | Source |
|---|---|---|
| → Hetzner FSN/NBG, OVH DE, AWS eu-central-1 (FRA) | ~1–15 ms | published-typical |
| → Singapore | ~155–180 ms | published-typical |
| → Hong Kong | ~175 ms | published: Dataplugs looking glass (Frankfurt→HK-DC) |

**Thai locations** — all international transit from Thailand concentrates
in Bangkok (SG/HK submarine gateways); upcountry sites pay only the
domestic backhaul delta on top of the Bangkok numbers.

| Site | → Thai DC (e.g. idc01) | → Singapore | → Hong Kong | → EU (FRA) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bangkok | ~5–10 ms | ~30 ms | ~62–70 ms | ~190–276 ms | measured (tony-dell uplink = Bangkok-metro routing) |
| Chonburi | ~6–12 ms | ~31–33 ms | ~63–73 ms | ~190–280 ms | estimated — Bangkok + ~1–3 ms domestic |
| Khao Yai | ~8–15 ms | ~32–35 ms | ~65–75 ms | ~192–282 ms | estimated — Bangkok + ~2–5 ms domestic |

## Candidate providers

| Provider | Relevant regions | Rough entry price | RTT class from TH (measured) | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Vultr** | SG, JP, FRA, … | ~$6–24/mo VPS | ~30 ms (SG) | Best price/perf for a Singapore node; per-hour billing |
| **Akamai/Linode** | SG, FRA | ~$5–24/mo | ~37 ms (SG) | Same tier as Vultr; predictable pricing |
| **AWS** | ap-southeast-1 (SG), ap-east-1 (HK) | Lightsail $5+, EC2 higher | ~30 ms SG / ~62 ms HK | Mature, but bandwidth pricing punishes chatty workloads |
| **DigitalOcean** | SG, FRA | ~$6–24/mo | no public ICMP target — expect ~30–45 ms SG (published) | Same tier; verify with their speedtest before buying |
| **Dataplugs** | Hong Kong (dedicated, CN2/BGP) | dedicated ~US$99+/mo | ~70 ms (HK) | HK dedicated/bandwidth-heavy role; overkill vs a small VPS |
| **Hetzner** | FSN/NBG (DE), HEL (FI), SIN cloud | €4.5–23/mo | ~276 ms (FSN, jittery path) | Best EU value; Asia-facing only via its pricey SIN cloud |
| **OVH** | FR/DE/CA, SG via OVHcloud | €4–15/mo | ~216–255 ms (FR) | Cheap EU; too far for interactive Thai use |
| **Contabo** | DE/SG/US | ~€5–11/mo | not measured; SG region exists | See prior assessment — CPU-steal caveat stands |
| **ReadyIDC / Siamdata** | Thailand | ~฿800/mo | ~7 ms class (idc01 measured) | The local pick — see prior assessment |

## Takeaways

- **Region beats provider.** From Thailand: TH ~7 ms → SG ~30–37 ms →
  HK ~62–70 ms → EU ~190–280 ms. Pick the region for the audience, then
  the cheapest reputable provider in it.
- **Singapore is the offshore sweet spot** for Thai/SEA-facing services;
  Hong Kong only if the audience includes China/Philippines north-SEA.
- **Philippines users**: HK or SG both land ~20–50 ms — a Manila DC
  (Zenlayer/local) only matters for sub-10 ms requirements.
- **Norway/Germany users**: EU providers (Hetzner, OVH, netcup, AWS
  eu-central-1) at ~5–35 ms; never serve them from SG/HK interactively.
- **For the idc02-class role** (batch, indexing, lab): EU value is real
  but the measured 190–280 ms hurts admin/interactive sessions — the
  prior report's "EU fine for batch" holds.

## Method & sources

- **Measured**: ICMP echo request ×3, averaged, from tony-dell
  (Thailand home uplink), 2026-10-07 evening +07. Endpoints that filter
  ICMP are listed as such — absence is not a down signal.
- **Published**: Dataplugs looking glass (dataplugs.com/en/company/looking-glass),
  Zenlayer Manila DC latency table, Tencent Cloud SEA latency matrix,
  OnionVPS Manila RTT estimates (great-circle floors), WonderNetwork
  Manila↔Singapore.
- **Estimated**: Khao Yai / Chonburi deltas and Norway→Asia figures are
  geography-based estimates, labelled as such.
- Single-evening, single-ISP snapshot — run provider looking glasses
  before committing spend.

---

sources: measured ICMP (tony-dell) + provider looking glasses/latency tables*

subject: idc01-return-dr-capability
title: idc01 returns — warm-DR node + measured failover capability

docs.contentMd:
## idc01 returns — warm-DR capability report (2026-10-06)

**Event:** provider kept the VPS; idc01 is back with previous specs
(2 vCPU / 31G RAM / 96G disk, public IP live, tailnet rejoined). It was
never wiped — the pre-migration stack was still running as zombie
duplicates of idc03.

### What was done

- **Zombie cleanup** — stopped+disabled the duplicated stack on idc01
  (ollama, gemini-ollama-proxy, camwall-edge, input-bridge, mddb-panel,
  obsidian-vault, vcast-headless@2/4). Old leader data dir preserved at
  `~/.config/containers/mddb/data.leader-retired-20261006`; the old
  `mddb.service` stays **masked** — never unmask it.
- **mddb follower #2** — new `mddb-follower.service` on idc01
  (:11123/:11124, `localhost/mddb:2.15.4-lsn`, seed = full snapshot pull
  from idc03). Image shipped idc02→idc01 via `podman save|load` (69MB).
- **Standby edge** — caddy-edge on idc01 now serves with the synced
  `api.surf-thailand.com` cert *pinned via `tls` directive* (ACME cannot
  obtain while DNS points at idc03 — this is the correct standby model).
- **Secrets backup deployed** — `secrets-backup.timer` daily 03:00 on
  idc03: age-encrypted tarball → idc02, idc01, tony-dell. Verified
  decryptable on all three (159 files each).
- **Warm-boot verified** — ada-pi-pwa on idc01 started and answered
  200 (envs already repointed to idc03 mddb); returned to standby.

### Measured DR capability (this session's numbers)

| Path | Measurement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Follower seed (snapshot) | connect → snapshot applied | **4m17s** (6.6GB, 88s verify on 2c) |
| Warm ada boot (idc01) | start → `/api/health` 200 | **181s** |
| Standby edge | `curl --resolve` TLS on idc01 IP | **works** (502 = no backends, cert valid) |
| Cold restore from backup | mddb.db → HTTP healthy | **>25min and counting** — vector index load on 2c dominates |
| Secrets backup | tar→age→verify→push×3 | **~4s**, verified decryptable on all targets |
| Estimated failover RTO | promote follower → ada up → DNS | **~8-10min** (unmeasured live, but each step timed) |

**Key finding:** the *replica* path (promote follower) is the fast
recovery — sub-5min data availability. The *backup* path on idc01's
2 vCPU is gated by vector-index load; HTTP doesn't bind until init
completes. Restore ordering: follower-first, backup as last resort.

### Found while working

- **idc02 follower stalled silently** — replication stream connected but
  stopped applying ~2h ago (confirmed_lsn frozen at 149.57M while leader
  hit 155M+). Restart resumed correctly *from persisted LSN* — the new
  `2.15.4-lsn` build's persistence feature validated under fire, but the
  stall itself is an mddb-fork bug to file.
- **vector-reindex exit-1 false alarm** — job succeeded
  (5 embedded, 12,299 skipped) but exits nonzero on transient conn drops
  during collection iteration; error classification nit.
- **idc01 standby envs already pointed at idc03** — migration env sync
  was more complete than recorded.

### New fleet shape

| Host | Role |
|---|---|
| idc03 | prod primary — mddb leader, ada, public edge |
| **idc01** | **warm DR** — follower #2 (promote target), standby edge, secrets copy #3, ada standby, lab sandbox |
| idc02 | heavy worker — builds, playwright/vcast, follower #1 |
| tony-dell | home hub — HA, board-api |
| tony-omen | GPU/dev |
| mn01 | light edge / standby alias |

### How dynamic are we now

- **Dispatch jobs: dynamic** — runner-agent claims by label/cap today.
- **Data: mobile** — 6.6GB replication in ~4min; promotion validated.
- **Services: scriptable-move** (~15-30min manual) — quadlets + state
  dirs are portable; clients still pin IPs (service-name indirection
  pending, card `service-name-indirection`).
- **Edge: manual failover** — standby edge removes most of the work;
  remaining step is the CF repoint.
- **Self-healing: none yet** — no autoscheduler; needs manifests +
  capacity scoring + a placer (staged, not urgent at this scale).

*Generated by devin session 2026-10-06 · sources: live systemctl/podman,
mddb /v1/replication/status, timed cold-restore + warm-boot*

subject: idc02-proposal
title: IDC02 Proposal

docs.contentMd:
# IDC02 Proposal — offload node for idc01

_2026-09-27 · Devin · measured on idc01 live (podman stats + service RSS)_

## Why

idc01 (Siamdata VPS, 2 vCPU / 12 GB / 100 GB) is saturated. Steady-state
usage is ~10 of 12 GB, and mddb alone consumes ~8.6 GB — enough that it
was in a cgroup-OOM crash loop today until its bounds were raised. Every
mddb restart wedges Ada's memory backend for minutes, and there is no
headroom left for Chaba Lab or any new workload.

## Current footprint (measured)

| Service | RSS (steady) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| mddb | **~8.6 GB** (rebuild spikes to ceiling) | memory/vector DB — the hog |
| ada-ha-tony | ~350 MB | production voice (latency-sensitive) |
| ada-ha-michael | ~110 MB | production voice |
| ada-pi-pwa | ~65 MB | PWA backend |
| open-notebook + surreal | ~340 MB | notebook stack |
| obsidian-vault | ~100 MB | vault sync target |
| ollama | ~10 MB idle / ~2 GB loaded | embed fallback (now unused — OR-only) + lab models |
| edge + proxy + panel + misc | <150 MB total | Caddy :80/:443 public edge, embed proxy |

## Proposed split

**idc01 keeps** (latency-critical / edge / small):
- Caddy public edge (:80/:443), input-bridge
- ada-ha-tony, ada-ha-michael, ada-pi-pwa (voice paths stay near the edge)
- obsidian-vault, gemini-ollama-proxy, mddb-panel

**idc02 gets** (memory-heavy / stateful / bursty):
- **mddb primary** (~9 GB working set, needs room to grow)
- open-notebook + surreal
- ollama (dev/lab models; embedding no longer needed — OR is primary)
- Chaba Lab when it deploys (was never viable on idc01 anyway)

tony-dell already runs an mddb binlog follower — with idc02 as primary
the replication topology stays intact and DR improves.

## Suggested spec (same provider — Siamdata)

**Recommended: 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB**

- 16 GB: mddb (9–10) + notebook (~0.4) + ollama (~2–4 loaded) + lab (~3)
  still leaves headroom; a 12 GB box would already be tight on day one.
- 4 vCPU: mddb's cold-start index build is CPU-bound — on 2 vCPU today it
  churned ~10 min per restart and starved all HTTP requests. 4 cores
  roughly halves that pain and gives the lab room to breathe.
- 150 GB: mddb.db + vectors grow; lab adds images/models.

**Cheaper floor: 2 vCPU / 16 GB / 100 GB** — works if the lab goes
elsewhere later; vCPU is the part that hurts least to start with on
Siamdata since upgrades are resize-reboots.

## Pros

- idc01 drops to ~2 GB used — ada voice + edge get a quiet, stable host;
  today's wedge-class incident disappears
- mddb gets real headroom + faster rebuilds; Ada memory ops stop being
  the failure-blast-radius of every restart
- Chaba Lab finally has a home without touching prod
- Same provider = same DC latency (~1 ms tailnet RTT) — mddb→ada calls
  add no meaningful delay

## Cons

- New monthly cost (est. Siamdata 4c/16G tier — check panel pricing)
- Second public IP = second thing to secure/patch; Caddy edge stays on
  idc01 so idc02 can be tailnet-only (recommended — don't expose it)
- Provider-correlated failure: one DC outage takes both (mitigated —
  tony-dell keeps an mddb replica)
- One-time migration: mddb.db + HNSW indexes move with ~30–60 min
  downtime, or replication-promote cutover (cleaner — seed replica on
  idc02, then promote)

## Suggestion

1. Order 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB on Siamdata, tailnet-only.
2. Bring up mddb as a replication follower first, verify, then promote —
  avoids a dump/restore window.
3. Move open-notebook + ollama after mddb is proven stable on idc02.
4. Keep Chaba Lab quota-capped there; re-evaluate idc01 sizing after a
  month — it may be worth downsizing to 8 GB once mddb is gone.

subject: jev-ai-assessment
title: Jev AI Assessment — measured v2

docs.contentMd:
# Jev AI Assessment — v2 (measured)

_2026-09-28 · Devin · reconciles pilot + model bench + Ada/GEV/Weaviate plan_

## Verdict

Jev (decision-only models, `/v1/systemone`) earns a permanent seat in the
stack — as an **async judgment tier now**, a **hot-path gate tier later**.
Local open-jev is live on tony-omen `:8777` (gemma-3-4b-it, CPU).

## Measured (3-backend bench, 18 real Ada decisions)

| backend | accuracy | latency | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| open-jev gemma-3-4b (CPU) | **83%** | 11.9s | calibrated — honest 0.559 on ambiguous turns |
| open-jev gemma-3-1b | 56% | 2.6s | too weak — under-scores plain "yes" |
| Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter | 57% | 1.4s | **uncalibrated — worse than the regex; do NOT gate through chat models** |

The `/v1/systemone` wire contract is backend-portable; the value is
logit-read scores. Chat models self-report confidence — structurally
fake calibration.

## Decision tier ladder

```
Tier 0  RULES      μs         gates, budgets, whitelists
Tier 1a JEV-async  ~12s CPU   post-turn audit, scenario judging, CMS classification  ← NOW
Tier 1b JEV-hot    ~400ms     confirm-gate, tool routing, ambient filtering          ← needs quant/NanoJev/hosted
Tier 2  GEMINI     streams    reasoning, generation, correction duty
```

Rule: cheapest tier that can hold the decision reliably. Each Jev win
removes a Gemini round-trip AND a failure surface.

## Ada↔GEV topology (as built)

- **Ada → `gev_command`** → `POST /command` (:8790) → function_call →
  GEV browsers — inherits Ada's full enforcement stack.
- **GEV's own Gemini session** in the bridge → 28 tools, **no confirm
  gate/budget/ops events** — the unguarded actuation path.
- Fix: thin guard shim in `gev-gemini/bridge.py` (budget + confirm +
  ops events) before any shared-gateway refactor.

## Data plane (unchanged)

MDDB canonical for Ada banks (Gemini-768 space, OR-Vertex primary —
cosine 1.000 proven). Weaviate stays dev-KB hybrid search (MiniLM
space). Different vector spaces — never merge; scope grows only via
retrieval bench data.

## Sequence

1. jev-bench committed → `tests/bench/jev-bench.py` emits
   `kind: benchmark` docs → auto-report catches regressions
2. Async Jev first: post-turn confirm audit, scenario judging
3. gev bridge guard shim (budget + confirm + ops events)
4. Retrieval bench: MDDB-vs-Weaviate recall@5 + latency
5. Hot-path Jev decision with bench numbers: 4-bit quant on the 1650 /
   NanoJev-0.6B trained on our transcripts / hosted API

`jev-weaviate-architecture-assessment.md`.

docs.contentMd:
# Unsloth for Jev model training — assessment

**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Context:** jev retrain dispatch (embedded + Thai affirmations)

## Question

Would [Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai) help re-train the Jev decision models?

## Short answer

**Yes — but only for the Gemma track.** Unsloth is a LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning
library for causal LLMs. The deployed confirm-gate student is
`distilbert-base-multilingual-cased` (an encoder classifier), which Unsloth
does not cover. Where it applies:

| Model | Path | Unsloth helps? |
|---|---|---|
| Student (distilbert-multilingual, ~135M) | HF `Trainer` seq-classification, GTX 1650, ~11 min | No — not a causal LM; already cheap |
| open-jev gemma-3-4b (teacher, bench-only) | zero-shot LM-head scoring today | Marginal — 4b QLoRA on 3.6 GB VRAM is right at the edge |
| **gemma-3-1b / gemma-3-270m "NanoJev"** | LoRA/QLoRA fine-tune for `/v1/systemone` | **Yes — the real win** |

## What it would buy

1. **A calibrated Gemma decision model instead of zero-shot.** Today the
   4b reads raw next-token log-probs ("yes"/"no") — accurate but
   uncalibrated, ~6–12 s/decision on CPU, and advisory-only.
2. **A full-API tiny model.** The attention-head route (used in this
   retrain — jevlike head over frozen 1b features) only answers `noul`.
   A LoRA-tuned gemma-3-1b/270m keeps `choice` and `score` working, still
   on the same wire API, so no consumer changes.
3. **Hot-path candidate.** gemma-3-270m (or 1b int8) fine-tuned could hit
   ~100–300 ms on CPU — inside the voice confirm-gate budget, where the
   4b never could be.

## Hardware reality check (tony-omen, GTX 1650 4 GB, sm_75)

- 1650 is Turing (same CC 7.5 as T4) — technically inside bitsandbytes /
  Unsloth support, but no fast flash-attn path; expect slow-but-works.
- **gemma-3-270m / 1b QLoRA:** comfortable (~1–2 GB VRAM, short prompts).
- **gemma-3-4b QLoRA:** ~3 GB weights + adapters + activations vs 3.6 GB
  usable — likely OOM unless batch=1, seq<=256, grad checkpointing. Doable,
  fragile.
- torch 2.14.0+cu130 already in `~/CascadeProjects/open-jev/.venv`;
  needs `pip install unsloth bitsandbytes peft trl` added.
- Unsloth is already in the pipeline indirectly: the gemma-3-4b-it
  weights in `open-jev/models/` came from unsloth's ungated HF mirror.

## Alternatives (what was actually done this round)

- **Distilbert student retrain** on merged corpus (live 1974 + mined 1205
  + reviewed verdicts + targeted aug for embedded/Thai affirms) — done on
  the 1650, golden 13/13, failure-set acc 66% -> 84%.
- **Torch port of the MLX-only `openjev features/train` head** —
  jevlike attention head over frozen gemma-3-1b hidden states (kk-macbook
  was unreachable, so the MLX path was unavailable).

## Recommendation

Worth one follow-up experiment, not a blocker:

1. Try `unsloth` QLoRA on **gemma-3-1b** (or 270m) with the same
   `train-all.jsonl` (context -> yes/no) on the 1650. If VRAM fights back,
   drop to 270m.
2. Bench it through `tests/bench/jev-bench.py` + the failure-case eval
   (`eval-all.jsonl`) before any `ADA_JEV_URL` change.
3. Keep the distilbert student as the production gate regardless — it is
   30 ms and already meets the bar; the Gemma models stay teacher/bench.
